Table rules (Joseph): reading him or lying to him is a contest. Catch him out: their Insight vs his Deception +12; they win, he lets something slip (d8, His slips in his doc); they lose but total 15+ or tie, he's choosing his words carefully. Lie to him: their Deception vs his Insight +14; they win, he believes them and favor doesn't move; tie, not fooled but favor doesn't move; they lose, he knows and favor drops. Elves roll both contests with advantage. His true name never slips.

The crew only sees him heal her. Each spiral is a time he brought her back; they can guess at that only with Arcana (DC 15: fae mending that went further than mending; DC 20: maybe called back from death). See the Captain Callomay document. He tells the crew: "If you ever see Thimble fall, bring her to me anyway. She is a tough fairy, and I don't expect anything will keep her down for long." She knew Vesperine of the Thorn (Rupert's patron) at court and won't say her name: "the Thorn Lady," then spits over the rail.

npcs.role: The rival explorer; captain of the Undaunted
npcs.where: Aboard the Undaunted (Hargrove House when ashore)

npcs.notes: Former Guild star; buys the wreckers' loot to pay for the Undaunted. WARLOCK 5 (2024): Human, Criminal background (Alert feat: + proficiency to initiative). Archfey Patron: his patron is Vesperine of the Thorn, an Unseelie archfey and the captain's rival at court for centuries, who wants Captain Callomay to lose his wager with Mother Brine - so the Sallowmay's crew must never finish a chart. She found him fifteen years ago, right after he broke his word to the captain (he and a teenage Fontaine crewed the Sallowmay; he sold a chart outside the Guild). Pact of the Chain: his familiar is a sprite, a spirit in a sprite's shape; Thimble can tell at a glance and it makes her furious. Invocations: Pact of the Chain, Agonizing Blast (+Cha to Eldritch Blast damage), Repelling Blast (push 10 ft.), Mask of Many Faces (Disguise Self at will), Misty Visions (Silent Image at will). Pact Magic: two 3rd-level slots, back on a short rest; Magical Cunning once per long rest. Steps of the Fey: Misty Step without a slot 3 times per long rest, with Refreshing Step (1d10 temp HP) or Taunting Step (DC 14 Wis save or Disadvantage against anyone but him). Archfey spells always prepared: Faerie Fire, Sleep, Calm Emotions, Misty Step, Phantasmal Force, Blink, Plant Growth. CR 3 is an estimate for the encounter budget, not a rule. Tactics: never fights fair - opens with Hypnotic Pattern or Sleep, blinks away with Steps of the Fey, and lets hired toughs take the hits. THE SILVER SWIRL (DM only): just peeking out above his collar. Captain Callomay saved his life when Rupert was one of his crew, fifteen years ago, and this is the mark it left, like Thimble's spirals. Rupert knows the captain saved him; he doesn't talk about it. Studying it is an Arcana check, read like Thimble's spirals (see the Captain Callomay document).

docs.md:
# Session 1: Hired in Kalatecha

Session 1 stays in Kalatecha and runs about 2 hours 20 minutes plus a break. It ends with the ship leaving the harbor at dusk. Everything has to happen in order, but any scene can shrink if you're running long. The fight in Scene 5 is the one to cut first.

Tick each part as you finish it. The run sheet at the top keeps the time, and the 📍 beside a part shows its place on the map; while this tab is open, every scene's place is numbered on the map. Read-aloud text is in the shaded boxes. Paraphrase it freely.

If you're running long at the break, play Scene 5 as a quick chase (about 10 minutes) instead of a fight.

## Before the players arrive

**Already settled:** the captain is [[npc:ln_callomay|Captain Callomay]] (true name Calandrous Callomaydare, DM only), with [[npc:ln_thimble|Thimble]] on his shoulder; his ship is the Sallowmay; the rival is [[npc:ln_hargrove|Rupert Hargrove-Vance]] of the Undaunted; the lantern seller is [[npc:ln_tobias|Old Tobias Pell]] and his gull Admiral. The crew: Xuna Kor'larym (Rebekah), navigator; Rin Amakiir (Elisabeth), medic; Ander (Benjamin), master-at-arms; Ethal Vaelor (Hannah), quartermaster.

- [x] Everyone has a character, with their sheet attached on the Party tab
- [ ] Each character is on the Party tab, with full hit points
- [ ] An index card behind the screen with each player's name and a favor score of 0
- [ ] Graph or hex paper with only Kalatecha drawn in, ready for Rebekah as navigator
- [ ] A lantern prop: a battery tea light in a jar works
- [ ] A sealed letter from the Charter House holding the commission (Scene 4)
- [ ] A blank notebook for the ship's log
- [ ] The Dock Ambush is ready in the app for Scene 5: six of Hargrove-Vance's deckhands
- [ ] The Captain Callomay document on the Docs tab, in case anyone starts investigating him
- [ ] Notes tab: click **Start session 1** in the Game log, so tonight's log stays together
- [ ] Snacks within reach, so the break is quick

## Opening {10 min} {place: kcity}

Put the city picture on the TV (top bar: **Players' screen** → Pictures → Show), or in the middle of the table, then read:

> The sun is warm on the red-tiled rooftops of Kalatecha, the free city by the sea. Tall-masted ships crowd the harbor, their sails patched with the colors of a dozen far-off ports. A stone fortress keeps watch over the coast. Above the market square, a great domed cathedral rises, and its bells ring out across the water.
> Kalatecha is where every voyage begins and ends. Sailors come home with strange spices, stranger stories, and maps of places no one has seen. Out past the horizon lie islands no one has charted: ruins, monsters, and peoples no one in Kalatecha has ever met.
> Each of you answered a notice on the longest pier, met its captain, and signed on. This morning, you report aboard.

Ask each player to point at one spot on the picture they'd like to visit someday. Remember their answers; they make good hooks for later sessions.

## Scene 1: Reporting aboard {30 min} {place: kcity/psallow}

The characters have already answered the captain's notice, and he's already hired them. This morning they report to the ship. Before he gives out the jobs, he asks each of them one last interview question; then he explains the four crew roles. Start by reading:

> The notice is still nailed to a post at the end of the longest pier. CREW WANTED. Honest hands for a voyage to uncharted waters. Ask aboard the Sallowmay. Since you last saw it, someone has written across it in neat, old-fashioned script: Positions filled.
> The Sallowmay sits at the end of the pier. She's not the biggest ship in the harbor, but she might be the best kept. Her deck is scrubbed white, her ropes are coiled neat as sleeping snakes, and every fitting gleams with polished bronze. A man leans on the rail at the top of the gangplank as if he's been waiting for you. On his shoulder sits a fairy no bigger than your hand, with dragonfly wings and a thimble for a helmet, looking you over as if you were fish at the market.

**Show the picture.** Put it on the TV: in the top bar, **Players' screen** → Pictures → The Sallowmay: hiring the crew. Two small clues are painted in: a sprig of hawthorn blossom growing out of the rail, and the silver markings on Thimble's arms. Don't point them out. If a player notices one, smile and move on.

**The captain greets them.** Read:

> "Right on time. Good. The sea doesn't wait, and neither do I." His eyes are the green of deep water, and his smile doesn't quite reach them. "You've all signed on, and I don't go back on a bargain. But before I tell you your jobs, I have one more question for each of you. Humor me."

**The last interview questions.** Go around the table. Each player gives:

- Their character's name and what they look like.
- Why they signed on. Are they after money, adventure, or getting away from something?

After each introduction, the captain asks that character one last question from the rail. Pick from these or make up your own:

- "What's the farthest you've ever been from home?"
- "Can you swim?"
- "What would you do if you found a treasure no one could ever trace back to you?"
- "Do you keep your promises?" (Note what they say. It matters for the favor track.)

Whatever they answer, he nods as if it's the answer he expected. Nobody fails this interview; he's learning who they are.

**The captain welcomes them.** Once everyone has answered:

> "Then welcome aboard. I'm Captain Callomay. The Sallowmay is mine, and she's the finest ship in Kalatecha, though I'm biased. You'll have a fair share of everything we earn, and you'll eat better than any crew in this harbor. In return, you sail her."
> "One thing you should know. I don't go ashore, and I don't go exploring. I stay with the ship. Out there, the decisions are yours."
> The fairy on his shoulder sniffs. "He means me too. I'm Thimble. Don't call me his familiar."

If anyone asks for his full name, he smiles and says, "Captain Callomay will do." If anyone asks why he never leaves the ship, he says, "Someone has to keep her safe." Don't explain further. His true name is Calandrous Callomaydare. Never say it at the table. If they ask about Thimble, he answers truthfully: "People call her my familiar. She calls herself my conscience."

**Crew roles.** All four roles are settled: Xuna (Rebekah) is the navigator, Rin (Elisabeth) the medic, Ander (Benjamin) the master-at-arms, and Ethal (Hannah) the quartermaster. They're already on the Party tab.

| Role | What they do | Good fit for |
| Medic | Keeps the crew alive and tends the sick and injured (Rin) | Clerics, druids, anyone good at Medicine |
| Navigator | Reads stars and charts and draws the crew's map (Xuna) | Anyone good at Survival or with a high Wisdom or Intelligence |
| Quartermaster | Handles supplies, money, and trading (Ethal) | Bards, rogues, anyone with a high Charisma |
| Master-at-arms | Leads in battle and keeps the ship's weapons (Ander) | Fighters, barbarians, paladins |

**The captain explains the roles.** Go around the table and read each part to the player who holds that role, handing over the prop as you go. From now on he calls each of them by their role ("Navigator," "Medic") until they earn their names. Start with:

> "A ship like this needs four people who know their jobs, and one who stays out of their way. That's me. So, listen."

**Navigator** (Xuna). Hand Rebekah the blank map with Kalatecha drawn in.

> "Navigator. You read the stars and the charts, and you tell her where to go. She'll listen to you, I promise. And you draw the map. Every coast we find goes on that page in your hand, not mine. I've never had the hand for it."

*DM only: the true reason is that fae ink won't hold a mortal coast. Don't explain it.*

**Medic** (Rin).

> "Medic. You keep this crew breathing. There's a healer's kit below, and it's yours now. Anyone who comes back hurt comes to you first, and that includes the ones who say they're fine."

**Quartermaster** (Ethal). Hand Hannah the ship's purse: **25 gold pieces, 33 silver and 65 copper.** It's the ship's money, not hers; it's written in her inventory in the app.

> "Quartermaster. The purse, the stores, and every bargain we strike. You'll know what we have, what we need, and what a thing is worth before anyone else on the dock does. Spend it well. Spend it, mind. A full purse never charted anything."

**The coins.** Nothing looks odd about them at a glance. If Ethal, or anyone, looks them over properly, they can make an Intelligence (Investigation) or Intelligence (History) check, DC 15. On a success: the coins were minted by three different countries, and only one of those countries still exists. The other two are gone, known now only from old maps and histories. (DM only: the sea pays him, out of wrecks from all over her waters and across three hundred years. No one ever sees him earn it.)

**Master-at-arms** (Ander).

> "Master-at-arms. When there's trouble, the crew looks to you. You keep the ship's weapons, and you decide when they come out. The locker's below." He hands over a small key. It's bronze, like every other fitting on the ship.

**Thimble** pipes up before anyone can ask:

> "And I'm the one who tells him when you're all doing it wrong."

**The captain finishes:**

> "Which leaves me. I keep the Sallowmay. I'll take you wherever you choose, and I'll be here when you come back. But out there, the choices are yours. All of them."

That last line is the bargain talking: only charts made by mortal choice count (see the Captain Callomay document). Keep it light, and let them decide everything.

**The ship.** The Sallowmay is her own place in the app. In DM mode, click her at the pier and press **Enter the Sallowmay**: inside are the [[place:kship/sdeck|Main deck]], the [[place:kship/squarters|Captain's quarters]] and [[place:kship/shold|Below decks]], and each one's **Enter this place** opens its map. Use them to show the crew around their new home, and for any fight aboard later. Anyone who searches the captain's quarters (they shouldn't, yet) can find the ship's log (DC 15) and, under the bunk, a sealed scallop shell (DC 20).

**Clue to drop.** When a player looks around the ship, describe the bronze: belaying pins, cleats, and the hilt of the captain's sword are all bronze. There isn't a scrap of iron anywhere on deck. Mention it once and move on.

**Send them ashore.**

> "We'll need supplies before we sail, and the Guild of Explorers has sent word that they have work for the Sallowmay. Go to the market, then to the Charter House. Bring back what we need, and bring me back whatever you hear."

**Favor watch.** This is the first chance to mark favor. Thanking him or complimenting the ship earns a +1 at the end of the night. Being rude to him earns a −1. Being rude to Thimble counts too; she tells him.

## Scene 2: The market {20 min} {place: kcity/ptobias}

The crew buys supplies and finds the lantern that burns without oil. Read:

> The market square is loud and bright. Stalls spill over with oranges, figs, and sacks of red and yellow spice. Gulls wheel overhead, waiting for someone to drop a fish. The cathedral's shadow falls across half the square, and in the cool of it, merchants sell things from far away: carved shells, feathered masks, a stuffed lizard as long as a rowboat.

**Supplies.** When the quartermaster tries to pay for food, rope, or water, every merchant waves the money away: "Already settled. Your captain's account." No one remembers him coming ashore to settle it. This is the second clue. Let it hang. (DM only: Thimble did it this morning, invisible. A player who makes a DC 15 Perception check spots a glint of dragonfly wings above the spice stall, gone in a blink.)

**The merchant.** At the edge of the square, in the cathedral's shadow, [[npc:ln_tobias|Old Tobias Pell]] sells salvage: coils of wet rope, a cracked compass, a figurehead with no face. He is a jumpy little man with a one-eyed gull named Admiral on his shoulder, and Admiral steals anything shiny. If anyone flashes a coin, Admiral grabs it and Tobias apologizes for him. Read:

> On a square of old sailcloth sits a brass lantern, its glass crusted with salt and tiny barnacles. Inside, a small flame burns a bright, steady gold. There's no wick and no oil. The flame just floats there, warm as a hand on your cheek.

Tobias wants 10 gold pieces for [[loot:ll_lantern|the lantern]] and won't say where it came from. He gets nervous if they press him. Let the players poke at it:

| Check | DC | What they learn |
| Insight | 10 | He keeps glancing toward the docks. He's scared of someone, not of the crew. |
| Investigation | 12 | The salt and barnacles mean it's been underwater for weeks. It came off a wreck. |
| Arcana | 12 | This isn't ordinary magic. The flame feels alive, and it always leans the same way, south, no matter how the lantern is turned. |
| Persuasion | 12 | He admits it came from a wreck on the southern reefs, sold to him by "people you don't want to meet." That's all he'll say. |

**Haggling.** A quartermaster who makes a DC 12 Persuasion check gets it for 5 gold pieces. If the crew is kind to Tobias and short of money, he'll let it go cheap just to be rid of it.

## Scene 3: The rival {15 min} {place: kcity/ptobias}

The rival explorer tries to take the lantern out from under the crew. Start just as the crew is about to buy it. Read:

> The crowd parts for a lean, silver-haired man in a fine Guild coat with the badges picked off. A monocle glints in one eye, a leather journal is tucked under his arm, and a swirl of silver just shows above his collar. Two broad-shouldered deckhands follow close behind. "Well, well." Rupert Hargrove-Vance doesn't look at you, only at the lantern. "Merchant, I'll give you twenty gold for that, and you can forget you ever had it."

**What [[npc:ln_hargrove|Hargrove-Vance]] does.**

- Offers double whatever the crew offers, up to 30 gold pieces.
- Talks down to the crew: "A ship full of new hires? How sweet. Does your captain let you hold the wheel?"
- Boasts about sailing first: "The Undaunted sails at dawn. Wherever that trinket came from, I'll be there before you've finished packing."
- Opens his journal and reads aloud: "Day one. New crew of the Sallowmay. Already overpaying for junk." He writes down every mistake they make, and says it out loud as he writes.

**His magic, just a glimpse.** He's a real warlock, and he doesn't want anyone to know it here. Give the table one odd detail and nothing more: the pages of his journal turn by themselves in a wind no one else feels, or Admiral shrieks and won't go near him. A player who makes a DC 15 Arcana check feels fae magic on him, cold and sharp, nothing like the captain's. (DM only: his familiar, Nib, a spirit in a sprite's shape, rides invisible on his collar. If Thimble is with the crew, she hisses at the empty air there.)

**Who gets the lantern.** Tobias sells to whoever treated him better, and the rival is rude to him. If the crew has been decent at all, he sells to them. If the rival does end up with it, the deckhands are carrying it in Scene 5, and the fight becomes about getting it back.

**As the rival leaves,** describe a look between the rival and the two deckhands. A player who makes a DC 12 Insight check catches it: the rival isn't done.

**Why the rival wants it (DM only).** He buys loot from the wreckers on Lantern Rock. This lantern slipped through and ended up in the market, and he wants it back before anyone traces it to the reef. Since the Guild stopped favoring him, that loot is how he pays for the Undaunted. There's more: his patron, Vesperine of the Thorn, an Unseelie archfey and the captain's old rival at court, wants Captain Callomay to lose his wager, so the Sallowmay's crew must never finish a chart. Stopping this crew is his real job. The players can piece this together over many sessions.

## Snack break {15 min}

Good stopping point: the crew has the lantern and knows it has a rival.

## Scene 4: The Charter House {15 min} {place: kcity/pcharter}

[[npc:ln_fontaine|Michael Fontaine]] hires the ship to chart Lantern Rock. Read:

> The Charter House of the Guild of Explorers is a grand building of pale stone with tall arched windows. Inside, every wall is covered in maps, and half of every map is empty. In the middle of the hall stands a huge globe. The parts no one has explored are painted with sea serpents.
> A tall, blond man in his early thirties hurries over. He's holding a stack of papers and has ink on his fingers. "You must be the new crew of the Sallowmay. Michael Fontaine, Guild of Explorers. Your captain's letter came this morning, so he's already said yes. Come, come."

**Another odd detail.** If anyone asks who delivered the captain's letter, Fontaine frowns: "It was on my desk when I came in. I assumed one of the clerks…" (DM only: Thimble, through the window. There's a tiny wet footprint on the sill, smaller than a mouse's.)

**When he sees the lantern,** he stops cold and lowers his voice:

> "Where did you get that? No, never mind. That's exactly why I asked for you." He unrolls a chart. Far to the south, a small island is circled in red. "Lantern Rock. There's a lighthouse on it that has shone every night for as long as anyone remembers, and no one lives there. Ships that follow its light don't come back. We've lost three this year."

**The commission.** Hand over the sealed letter prop. Then, in the [[place:kcity/pcharter|Charter House]]'s panel (DM mode), set the Lantern Rock mission on its board to **Taken**: that puts [[place:klantern|Lantern Rock]] on the sea chart as a known route, so the players see the way there. Un-hide the reef around it too, in its own panel. If you like, show them the board on the TV first ("Show it on the players' screen") with the job still marked Posted. The Guild offers:

- 50 gold pieces each to chart a safe channel through the reef and find out what happened to the lost ships.
- A bonus for anything valuable they bring back.
- A copy of the Guild's chart. Have Rebekah draw Lantern Rock onto the crew's map, about two days' sail south. The reef around it stays blank.

A quartermaster who makes a DC 15 Persuasion check raises the fee to 60 gold pieces each.

**If they ask Fontaine questions:**

- **Why us?** "Nobody else will take it. Well, Hargrove-Vance has been asking about Lantern Rock all week, which worries me."
- **Who is Hargrove-Vance?** "He was the Guild's best explorer, once. He thinks we owe him every job worth having. We don't."
- **Has the Guild sent anyone?** "One ship, two months ago, the Heron. She never came back."
- **Is it magic?** "I sit behind a desk now. Ask me about paperwork."
- **Why did he stop adventuring?** "I used to do this, you know. Then I discovered chairs."

## Scene 5: Trouble on the docks {25 min} {place: kcity/pambush}

Hargrove-Vance's deckhands try to take the lantern as the crew heads back to the ship. Read:

> The docks are busy with the end of the day's work. Cranes swing cargo nets overhead, crates are stacked higher than your heads, and the Sallowmay is just in sight at the end of the pier. Then three figures step out from behind the crates ahead, and three more behind you. You recognize the rival's deckhands. "We'll take that lantern," says one. "No need for anyone to get wet."

**The fight.** Use the [[place:kcity/pambush|Dock Ambush]] in the app: six of [[foe:lf_deckhand|Hargrove-Vance's deckhands]], built on the SRD Tough stat block. Its battle map is the docks: the pier to the Sallowmay, the crane with its rope and cargo net, two stacks of crates where the deckhands hide, a fish cart, and the warehouses behind. Everyone starts in place: the crew on the quay, three deckhands at the crates ahead and three at the crates behind. That's a Low fight for four level-3 characters under the 2024 rules: a warm-up. Keep it fast:

- The deckhands want the lantern, not a killing. If a character drops to 0 hit points, the deckhands grab the lantern and run instead of finishing them.
- When two deckhands are down, or when the crew has the lantern safe, the rest flee. Mark them Fled in the app.
- Let the master-at-arms decide whether to chase them.

**Things to use on the docks.** Reward players who use the scenery:

| Action | Check | Result |
| Swing on a crane's rope | Athletics or Acrobatics, DC 10 | Land anywhere on the dock, and get advantage on the next attack |
| Topple a stack of crates | Athletics, DC 12 | Everyone under it is knocked prone |
| Shove someone off the pier | Athletics against their Athletics or Acrobatics | They're in the water and out of the fight for a round |
| Drop a cargo net | Dexterity, DC 12 | One deckhand is tangled and can't move until they get free |

**Quick-chase version (10 minutes).** If time is short, skip the fight. One deckhand snatches the lantern and runs. The crew needs two successes out of three:

- Leap a fish cart: Athletics, DC 12.
- Cross a narrow gangplank: Acrobatics, DC 12.
- Spot the deckhand in the crowd: Perception, DC 12.

If they fail, the deckhand drops the lantern off the pier as he escapes. Someone has to dive in after it: Athletics, DC 10. Underwater, the lantern is still burning.

**Afterward.** Give the medic a chance to patch up the crew. Anyone who searches a fallen deckhand rolls Wisdom (Perception) in the app: each one carries the five silver he was paid, and one has [[loot:ll_hvnote|a note signed H.V.]] in his pocket (DC 10). A captured deckhand talks if treated well: "Hargrove-Vance paid us five silver each. Said it wasn't worth the trouble anyway."

## Scene 6: Set sail {10 min} {place: kcity/psallow}

The crew returns to the ship, and the Sallowmay leaves the harbor at dusk. The captain is at the rail when they come back. He asks what happened, and he listens closely if they mention the rival. Telling him the truth earns favor. Thimble wants every detail of the fight, and takes the side of whoever told it best.

Go around the table and ask each player for one thing their character does as the ship casts off. Some ideas by role:

- **Navigator:** Xuna sets the course south and pins the map to the chart table.
- **Quartermaster:** Ethal stows the supplies and counts the purse.
- **Medic:** Rin sets up a sick bay below deck.
- **Master-at-arms:** Ander checks the ship's weapons and keeps an eye on the Undaunted.

Then read:

> The sails fill and the Sallowmay slides away from the pier. Behind you, Kalatecha glows gold in the setting sun. Then the cathedral bells begin to ring. People on the docks stop and look up. It's not the evening hour, and it's not a pattern anyone in the city has heard before.
> At the rail, Captain Callomay closes his eyes and smiles as if the bells were meant for him.
> On the chart table, the lantern's little flame leans south, toward a lighthouse no one tends and a reef no one has crossed. Lantern Rock is waiting.

End the session there.

**The ship's log.** Ask who wants to keep the ship's log. That player writes a few lines tonight or before next session, and you'll read it aloud to open Session 2. In the app it goes in the Notes tab's Ship's log; "Draft from this session" gives them a start from tonight's game log.

## After the session

- [ ] Update each player's favor score on the index card. Note what raised or lowered it.
- [ ] Write down the spot each player pointed at on the city picture.
- [ ] Write down any names, promises, or details the players made up (the Notes tab works).
- [ ] Note who has the lantern and how much gold they spent.
- [ ] Ask the players what they liked best, and do more of it.
- [ ] Data tab: Download survey.json, and put it in the campaign folder's Saves folder.
- [ ] Notes tab → Game log → **Download session 1**, and give the file to Claude for a summary of the night.

**Session 2** opens with the ship's log, then the voyage south and the first scene on Lantern Rock: the false light.

# Reference

### Spotlight tracker

Each player should get at least one moment tonight where their choice changes what happens.

- [ ] Navigator (Rebekah, Xuna): reads the lantern's flame in the market, or draws Lantern Rock onto the map
- [ ] Medic (Elisabeth, Rin): patches up the crew after the docks, or wins over a captured deckhand
- [ ] Quartermaster (Hannah, Ethal): haggles for the lantern, or raises Fontaine's fee
- [ ] Master-at-arms (Benjamin, Ander): leads the dock fight and decides whether to chase

### Quick rules reference

| Situation | Rule |
| How hard is a check? | Easy DC 10, medium DC 15, hard DC 20 |
| Something helps or hurts | Advantage: roll two d20s and take the higher. Disadvantage: take the lower. |
| A character drops to 0 hit points | Death saving throws each turn: a d20 roll of 10 or higher is a success. Three successes and they're stable; three failures and they die. |
| A natural 20 on a death save | They regain 1 hit point |
| A natural 1 on a death save | Counts as two failures |
| A character dies | The captain's safety net: see "The rescue and the reveal" in the Captain Callomay document |

# Session 2: The False Light

Session 2 takes the Sallowmay out of Kalatecha on the night of day 1, across two days of open sea (with merrow at dusk on day 2 and a long rest that night), through the reef by the false light, and ashore on Lantern Rock as far as the ship graveyard. It runs about 2 hours 25 minutes plus a 15-minute break. Wreckers' Cove, the lighthouse and the firebird are Session 3.

Tick each part as you finish it. The 📍 beside a part shows its place on the map. **▶ Set the scene** (in the run sheet, and under each part's heading) does the setting up in one click: where the party is, the time of day, where the ship is, and the right map or battle map, with tonight's enemies already placed. The "In the app" steps below are there if you'd rather do it by hand. Read-aloud text is in the shaded boxes; paraphrase it freely. If you're running long, play one beat on day 2 instead of two, and skip the Sentry's Perch: the cove simply isn't warned.

## Before the players arrive

- [ ] Data tab: load the save "2026-10-13 kalatecha (session 1 XP, new rules)" (Load a survey.json). It has Session 1's XP by the new rules and the party aboard the Sallowmay at Kalatecha, night of day 1.
- [ ] Build mode, nothing picked on the sea chart: **This map → Road tools → Put places onto the roads beside them**.
- [ ] Notes tab (or the log on the left): click **Start session 2**. Missed checks can only cost XP earned after this, and "This session" on the leaderboards counts from here.
- [ ] Sea chart, the Sallowmay's voyage bar: **Sail to** Lantern Rock, **Stop every** ½ day (she'll stop at 10 in the morning and 10 at night). Don't sail yet.
- [ ] Sea chart, click the Undaunted: in her panel, **Sail to** Lantern Rock and **sets off in** ½ day (she leaves at dawn, as Hargrove-Vance boasted). Give her navigator a total of 12.
- [ ] Lantern Rock: check that the Sentry's Perch and Wreckers' Cove are still hidden, and that the octopus is in the Silver Tern.
- [ ] Decide the young stowaway's name. A suggestion: **Tamsin Pike**, ship's girl of the Heron, about twelve. Change it in the Library (People → The Young Stowaway).
- [ ] The crew's map from Session 1, for Rebekah to draw the reef on.
- [ ] Snacks within reach.

**A reminder about XP.** Every check you log in the Action box with a DC now earns XP (3 × level a point over the DC) or costs a little (half that, never below where they started tonight). A natural 20 that makes the DC is at least 50 × level, so tick **nat 20** when a player rolls one at the table. Healing outside a fight earns the healer XP. After each fight (the merrow, the octopus), **End the fight** opens the XP card.

## Opening {10 min} {place: kship/sdeck}

Read the recap. It's Thimble's version of Session 1, perched on the chart table:

> "Right. For anyone who wasn't paying attention, which was most of you." Thimble clears her throat. "Four fools answered the captain's notice. The captain gave them jobs, which was generous of him. They went to the market, bought a lantern that burns without oil off a man with a thieving gull, and let a fellow in a monocle try to steal it out from under them."
> "Then Michael Fontaine at the Guild gave them a real job: chart a way through the reef at Lantern Rock, where the lighthouse shines all night and ships don't come back. Somewhere in there a little spirit pinched a dagger, and nobody even saw it happen." She glares at the empty air beside her, as if it might be there now.
> "Then six of the monocle man's thugs jumped them on the docks. It went badly for the thugs. Ander knocked them into the harbor with thunder, and then knocked a few more in by hand." A sniff. "And someone tried to keep the lantern in her bag. I took it back. It's on the chart table, where it belongs, and the captain says no mortal made the light inside it."
> "So. It's night. The tide is turning. And Lantern Rock is two days south. Any questions? Good."

Ask each player for one thing their character is doing as the ship gets ready, at night, on the dock. Then move on.

## Casting off {10 min} {place: kship/sdeck}

The Sallowmay leaves Kalatecha in the dark, half a day ahead of the Undaunted. Read:

> Nobody hauls a line. Nobody climbs the rigging. The mooring ropes slip their posts by themselves and coil on the deck like sleeping cats, and the sails, pale in the lamplight, fill with a wind none of you can feel on your faces. The Sallowmay slides out past the Admiralty's walls. Behind you, the city's lamps shrink to a string of gold beads. Ahead, the sea is black and full of stars.
> At the stern, Captain Callomay rests one hand on the rail. "Navigator. South, if you please."

**The captain sails her.** He sails the Sallowmay by magic, all day and all night, and nobody needs to work the ship. If anyone asks how, he says, "She knows the way once she's told it." That's the truth, and all of it he'll say.

**The navigation check (your table rule).** Xuna makes a Wisdom (Survival) check to set the course. Put the total in the voyage bar's **Nav** box (tick **nat 20** if it was one), then press **▶ Sail**. The bar works out the time:

- A natural 20 halves the voyage: about a day.
- A total of 10 or more: the plain sailing time, about 2 days and 3 hours. They reach the reef in the small hours of day 4.
- Under 10: half a day longer for each point below 10.

You can also log the roll in the Action box (Survival, DC 10) so it earns its XP.

If a bad roll would bring them in by daylight, the captain heaves to a few miles off and waits for dark: the false light only burns at night.

**The lantern.** On the chart table in the captain's quarters, the lantern's little flame leans south and a little east. It never wavers. A navigator who watches it all night and makes an Intelligence (Arcana) check, DC 12, notices it leans a hair further every hour: it isn't pointing at a place, it's pointing at something that moves a little. (DM only: the firebird shifting on its perch in the cage.)

## Day 2 at sea {15 min} {place: kship}

The ship stops by itself at 10 in the morning (the **Stop every** setting). Pick two of these, then **▶ Sail** again.

**The fish that won't die (the quartermaster, or whoever likes fishing).** Someone fishes off the stern for supper. For each catch, roll a d6: 1 to 3, a bad fish (a reef bully, an egg-thief); 4 to 6, a good one. A bad fish can be cleaned and cooked like any other. A good fish won't die: the hook slides out of its lip without a mark, the knife won't cut it, it flops about quite happily until someone throws it back. If they ask the captain, he answers truthfully: "Nothing that doesn't deserve it comes to harm on my ship." A player who makes an Intelligence (Arcana) check, DC 15, recognizes old fae guest-law. (See "No innocents aboard" in the Captain Callomay document. The crew aren't covered: "You're not my guests. You're my crew.")

**The bird with the hook (the medic).** A storm petrel drops onto the deck, a rusty fishhook through its wing. It hops straight past everyone to the captain's feet and dips its head to him, the way a sailor ducks to an admiral. (A clue: sea creatures and seabirds treat him with odd respect.) Taking the hook out cleanly is a Wisdom (Medicine) check, DC 12. If Rin saves the wing, the petrel circles the masts and stays with the ship. Remember it: at dusk it shrieks a warning before the merrow climb aboard, and on the reef it flies ahead over the safe water.

**Iron below decks (the master-at-arms).** Ander takes stock of the ship's weapons. The locker is all bronze: blades, buckles, even the rivets. Then there are the three heavy crossbows and two maces Ethal brought aboard from the docks: plain iron. When the captain passes them, he steps around them the way you'd step around a puddle, and says, mildly, "Keep those in the hold, would you? Somewhere I won't put my hand on them." Don't explain. (DM only: cold iron is the one thing he can't touch. It matters again at the lighthouse, where the firebird's cage is cold iron.) The crossbows will be handy at dusk.

**Something big (anyone on watch).** Around noon, far off the port side, three dark humps rise out of a calm sea in a long line, and sink again without a splash. A player who makes a Wisdom (Perception) check, DC 15, sees a long head lift for a moment, look straight at the ship, and duck away. The captain lifts one hand from the rail, the way you'd wave to a neighbor. "She's only curious." (It's the same kind of beast the players' chart draws in the empty water. Some of them may be real. Who can say.)

## Dusk on day 2: the merrow {25 min} {place: kship/sdeck}

As the sun goes down on day 2, two merrow come up the hull, each with a red cap on its head. (Your table rule, from the Irish stories: the red cap is what lets a merrow walk on land.) In the app, pause the voyage (⏸) when the clock reaches dusk, about 7 in the evening, or set the time of day to dusk by hand. Read:

> The sun sinks into the sea ahead of you and turns the water the color of wine. The wind is soft, the ship hums along, and someone is already thinking about supper.
> Then the hull booms, once, as if something heavy struck it from below. Then again, nearer the stern. And over the rail on the port side comes a hand, long and grey-green and barnacled, with fingers as thick as rope, and then a second, and then a head: wide, flat, all mouth, with eyes like black glass. A rope-wrapped harpoon of yellowed bone rises out of the water beside it.

(If Rin saved the petrel, it shrieks and dives at the rail a heartbeat before the first hand appears: no one is surprised.)

The captain doesn't move from the wheel. Read:

> Captain Callomay looks at the thing on his rail, and for once he isn't smiling. "Those aren't curious." He doesn't draw his sword. "Master-at-arms. The deck is yours."

He doesn't fight: boarders aren't guests, but he leaves the fighting to his crew. Thimble shouts advice from the rigging, most of it rude, some of it useful.

**In the app.** First bring everyone up on deck: Where tab → **All together**, then put the party on the Main deck (anyone below decks climbs up the ladder on their first turn). Enter the Sallowmay and open the [[place:kship/sdeck|Main deck]] (Enter this place); it opens calm. In the battle panel, **Bring someone in**: two [[foe:lf_redcap|red-capped merrow]] (in the Library under Foes), against the party. Put them at the port rail, one amidships and one by the stern. Then **Start the battle**. Light: dusk, so everything on deck is in Dim Light. Two merrow are 900 XP, a Moderate fight for four level-3 characters under the 2024 rules: harder than the docks, and they have a long rest tonight to recover, so let them spend everything.

**What the merrow do (SRD 5.2, plus the red caps).**

- Two attacks a turn, any mix of Bite, Claw and Harpoon. A bite leaves the target Poisoned until the end of the merrow's next turn.
- **The harpoon** hits from the water at up to 60 feet, and pulls a Large or smaller target up to 15 feet straight toward the merrow. A merrow at the rail can drag a character across the deck and over the side.
- **The red caps** let them come aboard and fight on deck at 30 feet (they swim 40). Knock or snatch a cap off with Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), or a Strength (Athletics) shove, against DC 13, and that merrow is back to the SRD's 10 feet on land: it lurches for the rail and the sea. That's the clever way to win this fight, so reward anyone who tries it. Ethal's quick hands are made for it.
- When one goes down, the other dives and is gone. They're hunters, not heroes.

**Over the side.** A character pulled into the sea is in Deep water: swimming costs each foot of movement 1 extra foot. Climbing back up the hull is a Strength (Athletics) check, DC 10, or no check at all if a crewmate throws them a rope (an action). In the water, a merrow gets the swimmer to itself, so the crew will want to be quick.

**Things to reward on deck.**

| Action | Check | Result |
| Cut a harpoon rope | An attack against AC 12, or Ethal's knife as a Bonus Action | The pull fails, and that merrow has no harpoon until it dives for another |
| Swing out on a line to reach the rail | Dexterity (Acrobatics), DC 10 | Land beside a merrow and get advantage on the next attack |
| Drop a spar or a water barrel on a climbing merrow | Strength (Athletics), DC 12 | It falls back into the sea and loses its next turn climbing |
| Fire the iron crossbows from the stern | — | Heavy crossbows from the docks, if they kept them |

**Afterward.** Press **End the fight** for the XP card. Any cap left behind is [[loot:ll_redcap|a merrow's red cap]]: damp however long it's out of the water, and whoever wears it can breathe underwater (your table rule; it's in the Library). Very handy in the flooded hold of the Silver Tern. In the merrow's net, tangled with weed, is a tin locket on a broken chain, engraved T.P., with a tiny painting of a girl inside. Hold on to it: the stowaway on the Heron knows it (it's their father's; he's one of the sailors held in Wreckers' Cove). (A suggestion: change the initials if you rename the stowaway.)

## Night 2 and day 3 {10 min} {place: kship}

**The long rest.** The crew sleeps; everyone gets the benefits of a Long Rest (Party tab: **Long rest · everyone**). The ship sails on through the night by herself.

**Supper with the captain (a chance at favor).** Before they sleep, the captain has the crew to supper in his quarters, the first time he's done it. The pork is very good. If anyone asks, Thimble says the butcher swore that pig was "mean as a snake: bit his boy twice." Thanking him for the meal or the ship, or asking politely about his story, earns favor at the end of the night. Rin (−4) and Ethal (−9) both have room to win some back here; keep it generous. If they ask about Lantern Rock, he says, "I've seen that light from a long way off, for a long time. I've never been closer than I mean to be tomorrow night." He won't say more, and he looks south as he says it.

**Sails astern.** At dawn on day 3, the master-at-arms (or whoever is on watch) spots sails far behind: the Undaunted, following the same course and slowly gaining. A DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check makes out the monocle glinting at her rail. The crew is still about half a day ahead.

The rest of day 3 is quiet. The lantern's flame burns brighter the farther south they go.

## The false light {20 min} {place: klantern}

The Sallowmay reaches the reef in the dark, and the lighthouse blazes up. In the app, the voyage ends by itself when she arrives; set the time to Night if it isn't already. Read:

> The wind drops. The sea goes smooth and black as oil. Somewhere ahead, white water whispers over rock you can't see. And then, without a spark or a flicker, a light opens on the dark, high on a crag ahead: a great warm gold, brighter than any lamp, so bright it throws your shadows long across the deck behind you.
> It is beautiful. It is welcoming. It is exactly where a ship would steer for safe harbor. And somewhere in the dark below it, the sea is breaking on teeth.
> On the chart table, the little lantern's flame has turned to point straight at it, and it's burning twice as bright.

**The navigator's choice.** Following the light runs the ship straight onto the reef; that's what the wreckers built it for. The stars are the honest guide. Xuna makes a Wisdom (Survival) check, DC 15, to steer by the stars through the one safe channel. Help the table make it a crew effort:

- The petrel (if Rin saved it) flies ahead over the safe water: advantage.
- A Circle of the Stars druid knows these stars better than anyone; if Xuna uses Starry Form or reads the sky aloud, let it count.
- Rin, Ethal or Ander can call out breakers in the dark: Wisdom (Perception), DC 12. Each success adds +2 to Xuna's total. Elves and the drow see the white water first.
- The captain won't steer for them. If asked, he says, "Your choice, Navigator. It always is." (The bargain: only charts made by mortal choice count.)

**On a success,** the Sallowmay slips between two black reefs with a hand's breadth to spare and glides into the sheltered water off the east side. Rebekah draws the channel on the crew's map: the first safe chart through the reef, which is half of what the Guild is paying for.

**On a failure,** the hull grinds over rock with a long shudder. Everyone makes a Dexterity saving throw, DC 12, or takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage from being thrown across the deck. The ship limps into the same safe water, scraped and leaking, not wrecked. By morning the scrape has closed over, like bark over a cut. (A clue: the Sallowmay is grown, not built: willow and hawthorn, and she heals. Mention it once, at dawn, if anyone looks.)

**Reveal the reef.** In the Players' screen panel, brush the reef and the channel into view on the players' chart, or un-hide the reef shapes in their own panels.

## Snack break {15 min}

Good stopping point: they're through the reef, the light is burning above them, and the island is right there.

## Ashore {10 min} {place: klantern/lland}

The captain stays aboard, as always. Read:

> The captain lowers the boat himself and holds it against the hull while you climb down. "I'll be here," he says. "I always am." Thimble hesitates on the rail, then folds her wings and stays with him. "Somebody has to keep an eye on him," she says, which is not what her face says.
> You row toward a steep bank of shingle on the east side, the one place on the island a boat can come ashore. The stones crunch under the keel. Above you, bare rock climbs toward the lighthouse, and its light sweeps out over your heads, never down at you. Around the shoulder of rock to the west, in a lagoon between two stony arms, the dark shapes of ships lie tilted in the water, masts leaning like broken fingers.

**Go ashore in the app.** On the sea chart, press **⚓ Go ashore** (or open Lantern Rock and move the party to [[place:klantern/lland|the Shingle Landing]]). Its map is a beach. It's night: the drow and the elves see in the dark; Ander needs a lantern or a torch (there are lanterns aboard, and the ship has plenty of oil, oddly).

**Where they can go.** Show them the island from the landing: the cliff path up to the lighthouse; the lagoon of wrecks to the west. Let them choose. If they head straight for the lighthouse, the wreckers on the stair are the start of Session 3: let them reach the tower door and end the night there instead.

## The ship graveyard {35 min} {place: klantern/ltern}

A sheltered lagoon full of wrecks: three lost this year, older hulks under them, green with weed. Read:

> The lagoon is still and smells of salt and rot. Three ships lie in it, newer than the weed-black ribs around them: a broad merchantman broken across the reef at the mouth, her middle stove in; a smaller ship beached on her side at the head of the lagoon; and a third, picked clean, lying low in the shallows. The lighthouse beam passes over all of them and never lands on any.

**The Sentry's Perch (hidden).** On the west arm of the lagoon, under a scrap of sailcloth, a wrecker sits with a brass bell on a spar, watching the reef. If he rings it, Wreckers' Cove is warned for Session 3: the wreckers are ready, and the captured sailors are moved deeper in. Each character who comes near makes a Dexterity (Stealth) check against his passive Perception (it's on his sheet in the app). If they're spotted, he reaches for the bell: anyone within reach can stop him first. Ethal can silence him without a sound. A captured sentry is a fine source of information if he's treated decently. In the app, **un-hide** [[place:klantern/lsentry|Sentry's Perch]] when they find it.

**The Silver Tern and the octopus.** The biggest wreck, broken-backed on the reef, her hold half-flooded. Salvage is still aboard, and a [[foe:srd:giant-octopus|giant octopus]] lives in the hold. Use [[place:klantern/ltern|the Wreck of the Silver Tern]] in the app: its battle map shows the tilted deck, the broken mainmast, and the flooded hold where the octopus waits. Enter it calm, and **Start the battle** when it grabs someone. For four level-3 characters this is a Low fight under the 2024 rules: one big monster, lots of reach, and a chance to be clever.

- **What it does (SRD 5.2):** its tentacles reach 10 feet, and a Medium or smaller creature they hit is Grappled (escape DC 13) and Restrained while it's held. Once a day, when it takes damage underwater, it can fill the water around it with ink and swim off (Ink Cloud).
- **Good moves to reward:** breaking a grabbed friend free; fighting from the deck rather than wading into the flooded hold; using the broken mainmast as a bridge (Dexterity (Acrobatics), DC 10).
- **When it's badly hurt,** let it use its ink and jet out to sea through the broken hull rather than fight to the death. It's an animal, not a villain.
- **Afterward:** press **End the fight** for the XP card. Then the salvage: Wisdom (Perception), DC 10, finds [[loot:ll_salvage|the salvage]] (brass fittings, a ship's bell, a waterlogged chest of cloth) and the coin.

**The Marigold.** Stripped bare. Gouges in her hull show where crates were pried loose. A character who makes an Intelligence (Investigation) check, DC 12, finds a scrap of stenciled board: MARIGOLD. (A clue for later: the same crates are down in the Undaunted's hold.)

**The Heron and the stowaway.** A small ship beached on her side. In her hold, behind a wall of broken barrels, the [[npc:ln_stowaway|young stowaway]] has been living on hardtack and rainwater for weeks. Read:

> Something moves behind the barrels. Then a voice, thin and fierce: "Stay back. I've got a knife." A face appears over the top, sunburned, hair in salty knots, holding up a knife that is very clearly a spoon.

They're terrified, half-starved, and sure everyone is a wrecker. Winning their trust is the medic's and the quartermaster's moment: food, water, a blanket, a kind word. Wisdom (Insight) or Charisma (Persuasion), DC 12, or no roll at all for a good gesture. Rin tending them counts (and healing them outside a fight earns her XP). Once they trust the crew, they talk fast:

- The wreckers are "the queen's people." Raven Heartgrove. (Her look is still yours to decide. A suggestion for the stowaway to say: "She has a red coat, and she laughs all the time.")
- They live in a sea cave under the north cliffs. They keep the sailors from the wrecks there, roped up, "for ransom, they said."
- **If the crew has the locket from the merrow:** the stowaway goes very still. "That's my da's. He was bosun on the Heron. They took him to the cave." Now they have a name to rescue.
- "There's a stair. Cut in the rock, from up by the lighthouse down into the cave. They think nobody knows." (The stowaway can show them the [[place:klantern|Wreckers' Stair]], so no Perception check is needed to find it. Un-hide it when they do.)
- "A man comes in a ship with a gold figurehead. He has a glass in one eye. He buys what they take." (Hargrove-Vance.)
- "There's a bird in the light. I hear it at night. It sings like it's crying."
- What they want most: to get off this island. Taking them to the Sallowmay is safe; the ship's law covers guests, and the stowaway is one.

## Cliffhanger {10 min} {place: klantern/llight}

End the night with the island waking up. Pick whichever fits what happened:

- **If the sentry rang the bell:** torches spill out of a crack in the north cliffs, voices shout, and the lighthouse beam swings down toward the lagoon for the first time all night.
- **If they got through unseen:** the lighthouse light flares white for a heartbeat, and from the top of the tower comes a long, high cry, like a bird. The stowaway grabs someone's sleeve. "That's it. That's the bird."
- **Either way,** as the sky greys toward dawn, there are sails on the horizon to the north: the Undaunted, an hour or two out, coming in on the safe channel as if she knew it all along.

Read:

> The light at the top of the tower burns on, and for the first time you can almost see the shape inside it: something with wings, beating against bars.

End the session there.

## After the session

- [ ] Update each player's favor. Supper, the petrel, the stowaway: note what raised or lowered it.
- [ ] Note the stowaway's name and where they are (aboard the Sallowmay is safest).
- [ ] Note whether the cove was warned (the sentry's bell), and what the crew learned from the stowaway.
- [ ] Note the reef chart: did they find the safe channel, or limp in?
- [ ] Hannah wanted to see the cathedral in Kalatecha: save it for the homecoming.
- [ ] Data tab: **Save to the Saves folder now**.
- [ ] Notes tab → Game log → **Download session 2**, and give the file to Claude for a summary.
- [ ] Party & XP: show **Who is where** and the **Leaderboards** on the players' screen at the end of the night, if they'd enjoy it.

**Session 3** opens on Lantern Rock at dawn with the Undaunted coming in: Wreckers' Cove and the captured sailors, the spiral stair, the Lantern Room, Raven Heartgrove and Hargrove-Vance, the firebird, and the choice.

# Reference

### Spotlight tracker

- [ ] Navigator (Rebekah, Xuna): sets the course, steers by the stars through the false light, draws the reef
- [ ] Medic (Elisabeth, Rin): saves the petrel, tends the stowaway
- [ ] Quartermaster (Hannah, Ethal): the fish that won't die, the salvage, winning over the stowaway, silencing the sentry
- [ ] Master-at-arms (Benjamin, Ander): leads the deck against the merrow, the iron below decks, spotting the Undaunted

### Checks tonight

| Moment | Check | DC |
| Setting the course | Wisdom (Survival) (your table rule for time) | 10 for XP |
| Reading the lantern's flame | Intelligence (Arcana) | 12 |
| The fish that won't die | Intelligence (Arcana), to recognize guest-law | 15 |
| The petrel's hook | Wisdom (Medicine) | 12 |
| Seeing the beast clearly | Wisdom (Perception) | 15 |
| Climbing back aboard from the sea | Strength (Athletics), or a rope thrown (no check) | 10 |
| Swinging out to the rail | Dexterity (Acrobatics) | 10 |
| Dropping a spar on a climbing merrow | Strength (Athletics) | 12 |
| Knocking a merrow's red cap off | Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) or a Strength (Athletics) shove | 13 |
| The Undaunted's monocle | Wisdom (Perception) | 12 |
| Steering by the stars | Wisdom (Survival) | 15 |
| Calling out breakers | Wisdom (Perception), +2 to the navigator each | 12 |
| Thrown about on the reef | Dexterity saving throw, 1d6 bludgeoning | 12 |
| Sneaking past the sentry | Dexterity (Stealth) against his passive Perception | — |
| The mainmast bridge | Dexterity (Acrobatics) | 10 |
| Finding the salvage | Wisdom (Perception) | 10 |
| The Marigold's stencil | Intelligence (Investigation) | 12 |
| Winning the stowaway's trust | Wisdom (Insight) or Charisma (Persuasion) | 12 |

### Quick rules reference

| Situation | Rule |
| How hard is a check? | Easy DC 10, medium DC 15, hard DC 20 |
| Something helps or hurts | Advantage: roll two d20s and take the higher. Disadvantage: take the lower. |
| Darkness | The drow and the elves have darkvision; Ander needs light. In the app, the battle maps show what each character can see at night. |
| A character drops to 0 hit points | Death saving throws each turn: a d20 roll of 10 or higher is a success. Three successes and they're stable; three failures and they die. |
| A character dies | The captain's safety net: see "The rescue and the reveal" in the Captain Callomay document |

# Age of Exploration Campaign Notes

Oct 5, 2026 · @Joseph Crook

## Campaign overview

The crew sails out from Kalatecha, a bustling port city-state, to explore uncharted islands, mapping the unknown and bringing back treasure and stories. Each island is its own adventure; the city ties them together.

- **System:** Dungeons & Dragons, in an original setting built by the DM.
- **Players:** the DM's girlfriend (27), her brother (15), and her sisters (13 and 11). The three siblings have played about three sessions before; this is the DM's first campaign.
- **Tone:** swashbuckling adventure and mythical wonder. Islands are ruins, monster lairs, or home to peoples the crew trades and allies with — not lands to conquer.
- **Structure:** sail out, explore an island, come home to sell maps and resupply, repeat.
- **Table goals:** snappy combat, and every player gets a spotlight moment each session.

## The home port

Kalatecha is a sunny, walled harbor city-state where every voyage begins and ends. Tall-masted ships crowd the docks, a stone sea fortress guards the coast, and a great domed cathedral rises over a busy market square. Palm trees and terraced hills climb behind the red-tiled rooftops.

Show the players the city picture at the first session and let them point to where they want to go.

- **City name:** Kalatecha, an independent city-state.
- **City crest and flag:** set by the DM — the picture shows a real historical banner, so give the city its own.

## The main island

Kalatecha sits on the west coast of a large island, about 70 miles across and 125 miles from north to south. Everything beyond the city is hidden from the players for now. They can see only the first 5 miles of the southern road.

- **Who holds it:** the interior is its own country, with **Dunmarrow** on the north coast as its port. **Kalatecha** and **Saltmere** are free city-states. A possible plot point: two free cities trading past a country that surrounds them both.
- **Tolls:** each free city keeps a toll booth on every road out of it, with a hefty toll:
  - Kalatecha has three: Southgate Toll, Northgate Toll and Gullhaven Road Toll, each 10 miles out.
  - Saltmere has one: Saltmere Toll, 8 miles out.
  - **The toll (Joseph's table rule):** 1 gp a head and 5 gp a cart or wagon, each way, plus more on trade goods, at the DM's call.
- **Places:**
  - Cities: Dunmarrow (north) and Saltmere (south-east coast).
  - Towns: Briarford, Tallow Cross, Hollin's Rest, Greywater, Gullhaven and Thornwick.
  - Halfway House, a waystation.
  - Kalatecha Light, the lighthouse at the harbor mouth.
  - Nothing is inside any of them yet.
- **Land:** forest covers the island wherever there's no road, town or hill:
  - The Eastwold, Brackenmoor Wood, the Hollowheart, Gullhaven Wood, Thornwick Copse and Kingsfell Wood.
  - The Inland Hills sit in the middle.
  - The forest is hidden from the players too, because its gaps would show where the roads run.

## Key locations

Six places in the city, each with a job in the campaign. Names are placeholders.

| Location | Where in the picture | Role in the game | Hook or use |
| The Harbor | Docks, left side | Where the crew's ship is moored; every voyage starts and ends here | Overheard rumors, stowaways, suspicious cargo |
| The Admiralty | Stone sea fortress along the coast | Harbormaster tracks every ship; home of the armored city guards | Official warnings: "No ship has returned from the Ashen Isles" |
| The Charter House | Grand arched building on the plaza | Headquarters of the Guild of Explorers, who hire expeditions and buy new maps. Their goal: explore and turn a profit | A patron with a job starts each adventure |
| The Cathedral | Domed church with the tall bell tower | Main temple: healing, blessings before a voyage, a cleric NPC | Bells ring a special pattern when the crew's ship returns |
| The Market Square | Fruit and spice stalls in the plaza | Strange goods from distant islands turn up here | A merchant selling something no one can identify, like a lantern that burns without oil |
| The Upper Town | Villas on the terraced hills | Where wealthy sponsors live | Home of the rival explorer |

## Key NPCs

| NPC | Role | Description |
| Michael Fontaine | The crew's contact at the Guild of Explorers | Tall, blond, early 30s. A former adventurer who moved into middle management at the Guild because it's safer. |
| Captain Callomay | DM's NPC who owns and captains the crew's ship | A fully built character, a little higher level than the party. More part of the setting than an active adventurer: he hired the crew to sail his ship, never leaves it, and leaves the decisions to the crew rather than joining their exploits. The crew thinks he's a warlock with a fae patron; see the secret below. The crew knows him only as Captain Callomay. |
| Rupert Hargrove-Vance | Recurring rival from the Upper Town; captain of the Undaunted | A former Guild star who resents the Guild for handing its best jobs to newcomers like the crew. Wears a monocle and keeps a journal of every mistake the crew makes, which he reads aloud to them. Fifteen years ago he and Michael Fontaine crewed the Sallowmay, until he broke his word to the captain; his patron, the Unseelie archfey Vesperine of the Thorn, found him soon after (DM only; see the Captain Callomay document). Since the Guild stopped favoring him, buying the wreckers' loot is how he pays for the Undaunted. |

## DM only: the captain's secret

The crew believes the ship's captain is a warlock with a fae patron. In truth, he is the fae, and his true name is Calandrous Callomaydare. How each player treats him quietly shapes their luck, and they never see the score.

### Favor track

Keep a hidden score for each player from −15 to +15, starting at 0 (Joseph's table rule, 2026-10-10). Move it whenever his mood toward them changes; how far is your call. The wide scale leaves room for small shifts in mood without the effect jumping.

| Raises favor | Lowers favor |
| Thanking him for the ship or his hospitality | Mocking or insulting him |
| Including him in plans and celebrations | Ignoring him or bossing him around |
| Bringing him a gift or a share of treasure | Breaking a promise to him |
| Keeping their word | Lying to him |
| Asking about his story politely | Prying into his true name |

**What it does.** Outside of battle only, and only when you decide it applies, add the bonus (or penalty) for their score to a roll:

| Score | On rolls |
| +11 to +15 | +3 |
| +6 to +10 | +2 |
| +1 to +5 | +1 |
| 0 | No effect |
| −1 to −5 | −1 |
| −6 to −10 | −2 |
| −11 to −15 | −3 |

The Party tab shows each player's score with its bonus beside it, for example "favor +7 (+2)".

### Clues to drop

- The ship never seems to need repairs, and no one ever sees him pay for supplies.
- He won't touch cold iron; his sword and the ship's fittings are bronze.
- He never gives his full name.
- Milk sours when he's annoyed, and flowers open when he's pleased.
- Sea creatures and seabirds that come near the ship treat him with odd respect.

### Running it

- Keep penalties mild and rewards generous, so the youngest player isn't punished for a joke.
- Let players notice the pattern on their own; never confirm it.
- Save the reveal for a big moment, such as when the crew stands up for him or badly betrays him.
- **Safety net:** if a character dies, especially the youngest player's, the captain appears out of thin air beside them and brings them back. It is the only time he ever leaves the ship, and that rescue doubles as the reveal. Use it only once, keep it open to any player, and consider a small fae price, like a favor owed or a silver mark on the skin.

## The crew and ship

The ship belongs to the captain, who hires the players as his crew: they run it and map the world from its deck.

- **Ship name:** the Sallowmay, the captain's ship.
- **Crew roles:** each player takes one of medic, navigator, quartermaster, or master-at-arms (the crew's fighter, who leads in battle and keeps the ship's weapons). The DM plays the ship's captain and patron, an NPC who owns the ship and hires the crew. He never leaves the ship and leaves the decisions to the crew. Roles give everyone a job and a reason to care about the ship.
- **The blank map:** hand the players graph or hex paper with only the home port drawn in. As they sail, they draw coastlines, name islands, and mark dangers.
- **Ship's log:** one player writes a few lines after each session; read it aloud to recap at the start of the next.
- **Sailing time:** the captain sails the Sallowmay by magic, 24 hours a day, with no crew needed. At a sailing ship's 2 mph that's about 48 miles a day, or half that against a strong wind.
- **Navigation check (table rule):** before each voyage the navigator makes a check. A natural 20 halves the voyage time; a total under 10 adds half a day for each point below 10.
- **New islands:** an island goes on the players' chart as a route when the crew gets a mission there. Anything else turns up when the ship comes within about 10 miles of it.

Role holders:

- [x] Medic: Rin Amakiir (Elisabeth)
- [x] Navigator: Xuna Kor'larym (Rebekah)
- [x] Quartermaster: Ethal Vaelor (Hannah)
- [x] Master-at-arms: Ander (Benjamin)
- [x] Ship's captain and patron (DM's NPC), name: Captain Callomay

## Session 1 plan

Session 1 stays in the city so the DM can find their footing and the players warm up with low stakes, and ends with the ship leaving the harbor.

- **Meet the crew.** Each player introduces their character. They report aboard the captain's ship, already hired; he asks each a last interview question, then gives them their crew roles.
- **The market.** The crew explores the market square. A merchant has a strange item from an unknown island and won't say where it came from.
- **The rival.** A cocky rival explorer from the upper town shows up, wants the same item, and boasts about sailing first.
- **The job.** Michael Fontaine of the Guild of Explorers offers a commission: chart the island the item came from and bring back proof.
- **A small challenge.** A short scuffle on the docks or a chase through the market refreshes combat and ability checks.
- **Set sail.** End the night with the cathedral bells ringing as the ship leaves the harbor.

Aim for 2 to 3 hours with snack breaks. Give each player at least one moment where their choice changes what happens.

## The first voyage and beyond

The first island is an original one, built by the DM to fit the campaign's vibe and tied to the strange item from the market.

- **First island:** keep it small — a handful of locations, one or two fights, one mystery or puzzle, and a clear prize to bring home. It's the island the market item came from.
- **Coming home:** after each island, the crew returns to the home port to sell their map, heal, resupply, and pick up the next rumor.
- **Later islands:** Ghosts of Saltmarsh adds rules for ships, sailing, and naval combat, plus seafaring adventures to drop in as new islands or ports. It was written for the 2014 rules but works alongside the newer ones.
- **The rival explorer:** shows up every few islands, sometimes ahead of the crew, sometimes needing rescue. Gives the campaign a throughline without heavy plotting.
- **Island ideas to fill in:** ruins of a lost people, a monster's lair, a friendly island to trade with, a place that isn't on any map.

## First island: Lantern Rock

A lonely island whose lighthouse has shone every night for as long as anyone remembers, though no one lives there. Ships that follow its light don't come back. It should take 2 to 3 sessions.

**The secret.** The light is a firebird, a great flame-feathered bird locked in an iron cage at the top of the lighthouse. The cage is cold iron, the one thing the captain can't touch: he won't ask the crew to free it, but he'll be very glad if they do. Wreckers led by the pirate queen Raven Heartgrove use its light to lure ships onto the reef, then loot the wrecks. The rival explorer buys their loot, and now wants the firebird itself.

**The hook.** The merchant's strange item is a lantern that burns without oil, salvaged from a wreck on the reef. Three ships have vanished near Lantern Rock this year. Michael Fontaine hires the crew to chart a safe channel through the reef and find out what happened, with a bonus for anything valuable they bring back.

### Scenes

- **The false light.** Night falls as the ship nears the reef, and the lighthouse blazes to life. The navigator must trust the stars over the light; following it runs the ship onto the rocks. Failure means a scraped hull and a rough landing, not disaster.
- **The ship graveyard.** A lagoon full of wrecks to search for loot and clues. A giant octopus lives in the biggest one. A young stowaway who survived a wreck is hiding here and tells the crew about the wreckers.
- **Wreckers' Cove.** The pirates' camp sits in sea caves below the cliffs, with sailors from the lost ships held for ransom. The crew can sneak in, bluff, or fight.
- **The lighthouse.** A spiral stair climbs the cliff tower. At the top, Raven Heartgrove and the rival are haggling over the caged firebird. Big swashbuckling fight on the stairs and in the lantern room: swinging from the great lamp's chains and knocking pirates off the gallery into the sea.
- **The choice.** The firebird can be freed or sold. The Guild would pay a fortune for it. Freed, it bursts into the sky, lights a safe path through the reef, and leaves the crew a feather that never stops glowing.
- **Escape.** With the cove in uproar, the crew gets the rescued sailors back to the ship while the rival slips away.

**The prize.** The first safe chart of the reef for the Guild, loot from the wrecks, grateful sailors with friends back in Kalatecha, and either a fortune or a firebird feather, depending on their choice.

### On the map

Lantern Rock is a jagged, barren island about 240 yards across: bare stone and shingle, a lagoon of wrecks between two rocky arms, and reefs all round. Open [[place:klantern|Lantern Rock]] on the sea chart to go inside. Each place has its own battle map.

| Place | What happens there | Fight (level 3) |
| [[place:klantern/lland|The Shingle Landing]] | The one safe place to come ashore, on the east side. The cliff path climbs from here to the lighthouse. | None |
| [[place:klantern/ltern|Wreck of the Silver Tern]] | The biggest wreck, broken on the reef at the lagoon's mouth. The giant octopus waits in her flooded hold. Salvage is still aboard. | 1 giant octopus |
| [[place:klantern/lheron|Wreck of the Heron]] | The young stowaway hides in her hold. | None |
| [[place:klantern/lmarigold|Wreck of the Marigold]] | Stripped bare. Her cargo is in the Undaunted's hold. | None |
| [[place:klantern/lsentry|Sentry's Perch]] (hidden) | A wrecker watches the reef. If he rings his bell, the cove is warned. | 1 wrecker |
| [[place:klantern/lcove|Wreckers' Cove]] (hidden) | The pirates' camp in a sea cave under the north cliffs. The captured sailors are in a barred pen. The strongbox is in the queen's nook (Perception DC 15 to find). | 3 wreckers, 1 bruiser |
| [[place:klantern/llight|The Lighthouse]] | The base of the tower and its narrow spiral stair, held by wreckers. They come at the crew a few at a time. | 4 wreckers, 1 bruiser (Low) |
| [[place:klantern/llamp|The Lantern Room]] | The top of the tower: Raven Heartgrove and Hargrove-Vance haggling over the caged firebird, the gallery high over the sea. Hargrove-Vance slips away rather than fight. | Raven Heartgrove, 2 wreckers, 1 bruiser (Low) |

The Wreckers' Stair, a hidden way cut in the rock from the lighthouse crag down to the cove, is hidden from the players too. Finding it takes Wisdom (Perception) DC 15, or the stowaway can show them.

### Spotlight moments

| Crew role | Their moment |
| Navigator | Trusts the stars over the false light and steers the safe channel through the reef/maps the island |
| Medic | Tends the rescued sailors, or soothes the injured firebird so it can fly |
| Quartermaster | Sorts out what's valuable in the wrecks, or bluffs the wreckers into a deal |
| Master-at-arms | Leads the charge up the lighthouse stairs and duels Raven Heartgrove |

For monsters, look for giant octopus, pirate or bandit, and bandit captain stat blocks in the rules. The firebird doesn't need stats; it's a prize, not a fight.

## Materials checklist

- [ ] The D&D rules: the free rules on D&D Beyond, or the 2024 Player's Handbook
- [ ] A set of dice for each player
- [ ] Dry-erase battle mat and markers
- [ ] Graph or hex paper for the players' map
- [ ] Index cards and pencils
- [ ] DM screen (a standing folder works)
- [ ] Props: a tea-stained "old map," a sealed letter from the Charter House, a notebook for the ship's log
- [ ] Snacks
- [ ] Later: Ghosts of Saltmarsh
- [ ] Later: 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide

## Still to decide

- [ ] What's on Kalatecha's flag?
- [ ] Who leads the Guild of Explorers?
- [x] The pirate queen's name: Raven Heartgrove.
- [ ] What does each player want their character to be?
- [ ] Date and length of session 1.
- [ ] What's the inland country called, and who rules it?
- [ ] How do the free cities and the inland country get along?
