# Captain Callomay

Oct 7, 2026 · Joseph Crook

DM only. The captain of the Sallowmay, as the crew knows him and as he really is: his numbers for when the players start investigating him, what each kind of snooping turns up, and his story.

## At a glance

| **What the crew sees** | Captain Callomay, owner and captain of the Sallowmay. Lean and unhurried, eyes the green of deep water, a smile that doesn't quite reach them, a bronze-hilted sword. Courteous, dry, a little sad. A fairy named Thimble rides on his shoulder. Everyone assumes he's a warlock with a fae patron and that she's his familiar, and he lets them. |
| **What he really is** | An archfey: Calandrous Callomaydare, once called the Lord of Far Shores. The warlock is a costume. There is no patron. He is the fae. |
| **What he wants** | To pay off a wager he lost to the sea three hundred years ago, so he can stand on dry land again. |
| **What he fears** | That he'll outlive this crew too. And, quietly, that when he's finally free he'll miss the sea. |
| **Voice** | Unhurried and courteous. Calls the crew by their roles ("Navigator", "Medic") until they earn their names. Answers questions with questions when he'd rather not answer. |
| **Rules he can't break** | He never tells an outright lie. He can't set foot on land. He can't touch cold iron. He can't draw a map of a mortal coast. He keeps every bargain he makes, to the letter. |
| **The ship's rule** | No innocent can be harmed aboard the Sallowmay, and nothing innocent ends up on her table. The crew aren't covered: they're crew, not guests. See No innocents aboard. |

## His numbers

He never rolls to fight. Fights around him are narrative (see Running him in a fight). These numbers are for the moments the players test him: lying to him, sneaking past him, studying him. They're my homebrew numbers for an archfey, not a stat block from the rules.

| **Str** | **Dex** | **Con** | **Int** | **Wis** | **Cha** |
| 12 (+1) | 18 (+4) | 16 (+3) | 18 (+4) | 20 (+5) | 24 (+7) |

| **Proficiency bonus** | +6 |
| **Saving throws** | Dex +10, Wis +11, Cha +13; the rest use the ability modifier |
| **Skills** | Deception +12, Insight +14 (both tuned so the crew has a real chance against him; see When they investigate him), History +16, Performance +13, Persuasion +13, Perception +11, Survival +11, Arcana +10, Sleight of Hand +10, Stealth +10 |
| **Passive Perception** | 21 |
| **Passive Insight** | 24. When the crew lies to him or tries to read him, roll instead: see When they investigate him. |
| **Senses** | On the Sallowmay he knows everything that happens aboard, as if the ship tells him. |
| **Languages** | Every language anyone has ever spoken at sea. He pretends not to understand some of them. |

## The warlock act

He never claims to be a warlock. Other people say it, and he doesn't correct them. Everything he says about it is true, just carefully worded:

> "People say I made a pact with a fae. I made a bargain, yes. I've been paying for it ever since."

> "Who do I serve? The sea. She's the oldest of them all. The sailors call her Mother Brine."

> "My price? Maps. Every true chart you draw takes a little off what I owe."

Small magic he does in plain view, which looks like a warlock's tricks: a lantern lights when he touches it, ropes knot themselves, a breeze comes when he whistles, fog parts in front of the bow, and spilled water runs back into its cup. He never needs to roll for any of it.

And every warlock story has a familiar, so the crew will assume Thimble is his. She isn't (see Thimble, below). Asked about her, he tells the truth:

> "People call her my familiar. She calls herself my conscience."

> "I don't command Thimble. I ask, and most days she says yes."

## Thimble, the fairy who isn't a familiar

A sprite no bigger than a hand: dragonfly wings, a sewing needle for a sword, a thimble for a helmet. Silver markings wind around both her arms: spirals and triskelions, like old druidic knotwork. (DM only: one for each time the captain has brought her back to life. The crew doesn't know that: as far as they can tell, he heals her. See Study her silver spirals.) Bossy, nosy and fiercely loyal. She calls the captain "Callo" and the crew "the new ones." She was part of his court in the old days, helped plant the willow and the hawthorn the Sallowmay grew from, and followed him to sea when he lost the wager. Nobody ordered her to.

**What she does for him.** He can't set foot on land, so Thimble goes ashore for him: she's his eyes on the docks, his ears in the taverns, and the one who brings back gossip. She can't draw maps any more than he can; fae ink won't hold a mortal coast. When he wants to know whether someone is honest, he asks Thimble, who has looked at their heart (her Heart Sight).

**Her numbers.** Use the SRD Sprite stat block; it's on her sheet in the app. AC 15, 10 hit points, speed 10 feet and fly 40 feet. Needle Sword (+6, 1d4 + 4 piercing). Enchanting Bow (+6, 1 piercing, and the target is Charmed until the start of her next turn). Heart Sight (a creature within 5 feet makes a DC 10 Charisma save or she learns its emotions and alignment). She can turn invisible at will. She counts as crew, not a guest, so the ship's rule doesn't protect her either.

**If she falls (Joseph's table rule).** Ten hit points doesn't last long, and she's too important to lose. At 0 hit points she's dead, but not for good: if the crew brings her to the captain, he brings her back. As far as the crew can tell, he heals her: he takes her into his cabin, and she comes out a few hours later, grumbling, with one more silver spiral on her arm. Nobody says the word "dead." He tells the crew early, so they know to carry her home:

> "If you ever see Thimble fall, bring her to me anyway. She is a tough fairy, and I don't expect anything will keep her down for long."

He never has to leave the ship to do it, so it doesn't break his bargain the way the rescue does (see The rescue and the reveal). If the crew asks whether he could heal them the same way, he changes the subject.

**How she gives the game away.** A real familiar comes from the Find Familiar spell, and the spell sets rules she keeps breaking. Players who know the rules can catch it:

| **A real familiar (Find Familiar)** | **Thimble** |
| **A spirit wearing an animal's shape.** | A real fey, flesh and wings. |
| **Obeys its master's commands.** | Argues with him in front of everyone, and sometimes says no. |
| **Can't attack.** | Draws her needle sword on anyone who threatens him. |
| **At 0 hit points it disappears, dropping whatever it carried, until the spell is cast again.** | Hurt, she bleeds like anyone else. She doesn't vanish. When she falls, her body stays, and it's the captain who mends her, not a spell. |
| **Its master talks to it in their mind within 100 feet, and can see through its eyes.** | They talk out loud. She flies ashore for a whole day and reports back in person. |
| **Its master can send it away to a pocket dimension.** | When she wants to be gone, she just turns invisible. |

## When they investigate him

**He never lies, but he hides a great deal.** When they try to read him or to lie to him, it's a contest: they roll, he rolls, and the higher total wins. That's the fun of it: the kids can piece together that he's hiding something, and bit by bit what, without ever being handed it.

These numbers are tuned for the table (my call, not the rules). His Deception is +12 and his Insight +14, so his roll averages about 23 when they try to read him and about 25 when they lie to him: he is harder to fool than to read. A good roll has a real chance against him, but beating him should feel like a win. **Elves roll these two contests with advantage** (my rule): they have fey blood, and they can read one of their own. Rin and Xuna are elves.

How often they win, for a player at +4: reading him, about 1 time in 6 (an elf, rolling with advantage, about 1 in 4); lying to him, about 1 time in 9 (an elf, about 1 in 5).

| **They try to** | **Roll** | **What they learn** |
| **Catch him out** | Their Wisdom (Insight) against his Charisma (Deception), +12 | **They win:** he lets something slip. Roll on His slips, below. **They lose, but their total is 15 or more, or it's a tie:** "He's choosing his words very carefully. He answered a slightly different question than the one you asked." **They lose with under 15:** he seems completely sincere, which he is. |
| **Lie to him** | Their Charisma (Deception) against his Wisdom (Insight), +14 | **They win:** he believes them, this time, and favor doesn't move. **Tie:** he isn't fooled, but he lets it go, and favor doesn't move. **They lose:** he knows. He doesn't say so, and lying to him lowers favor, as in the campaign notes. |
| **Sneak or pickpocket on the ship** | Dex (Stealth or Sleight of Hand) vs his passive Perception 21 | The ship tells him. The first time, he finds it funny and returns what was taken. After that it counts as breaking his trust. |
| **Study his magic** | Intelligence (Arcana), DC 15 | A warlock's magic comes through a pact, and pacts leave a mark: a sigil, a token, a voice in their head. He has none, and the fairy on his shoulder isn't one either (see Study Thimble). "The magic doesn't come through him. It comes from him." DC 20: it's fae magic, older than any pact. |
| **Study Thimble** | Intelligence (Arcana), DC 15 | She's no familiar. A familiar is a spirit wearing a borrowed shape, and it does as it's told. Thimble is a real sprite, and she argues with him. DC 20: she's from a fae court, and she serves him the way a courtier serves a lord, by her own choice. |
| **Win Thimble over** | Charisma (Persuasion), DC 15 | She never tells his secret, but she lets one true thing slip: "I knew him when he had a garden." Call her his familiar and she's insulted: "I am not his pet. I'm his..." and she stops. No roll needed for that part. |
| **Study her silver spirals** | Intelligence (Arcana), DC 15 | They can tell what the spirals might be, never for certain. **15 or more:** they look druidic, but they aren't: this is fae magic, very old and very strong, the kind of mark mending leaves when it went much further than mending. **20 or more:** stories say marks like these are left on someone who was called back from very far away. Maybe from death. If that's true, she has been there as many times as there are spirals. **Under 15:** silver spirals and triskelions, like old druidic knotwork. Pretty, and probably decoration. (Xuna, a druid, would recognize the style, not the magic.) Thimble catches them looking and pulls her sleeves down. |
| **Cast Detect Magic on him** | None | Illusion magic clings to his face and hands (his human look is a glamour). The whole ship glows faintly too: hull, rigging and figurehead, but not the cargo or the crew's own things. |
| **Remember fae lore** | Intelligence (Arcana or Nature), DC 15 | Fae can't abide cold iron. They don't lie, but they twist words. Names hold power. A bargain with a fae binds both sides. DC 20: even fae can be bound, by bargains with powers older than they are. |
| **Search [[place:kship/squarters|his cabin]]** | Intelligence (Investigation), DC 15 | The ship's log, written in dozens of different hands, crew after crew, the oldest pages so faded the ink is nearly gone. Counts as prying if he finds out (he will). |
| **Search it thoroughly** | Intelligence (Investigation), DC 20 | Under the bunk, a sealed scallop shell. Inside, a strand of kelp tied in a knot that won't come undone. Arcana DC 20 recognizes it: a bargain, still binding. |
| **Dig through city records** | Intelligence (History), DC 15, or ask Commodore Quell | The Admiralty's registry lists the Sallowmay in every ledger back to the city's founding. The captain is always written down as "Captain C." |
| **Hand him something iron** | Wisdom (Insight), DC 10 | He declines it gracefully, but there's a flicker of real distaste, like someone offered a dead fish. |
| **Ask him about his story, politely** | None | He tells them a sea story: the warlock act above, or the tale of the wager told as if it happened to someone else. Raises favor, as in the campaign notes. |

### His slips

When someone beats him in the contest to catch him out, roll a d8 (or pick one that fits the moment). Each points at his secret without giving it away. Once a slip has come up, he's careful about it afterwards, so reroll repeats.

| **d8** | **The slip** |
| **1** | "The last time I walked on a beach…" He stops, and changes the subject. (He hasn't stood on land in a very long time.) |
| **2** | He speaks of Mother Brine as "the old girl," fondly and a little bitterly, the way you'd speak of someone you've met. |
| **3** | Asked his age: "Older than the harbor wall." The harbor wall is two hundred years old; Commodore Quell can confirm it. |
| **4** | He corrects a detail in a sea story no one living could know: "No, she went down on the north side. There were gulls." |
| **5** | Something iron brushes his sleeve. He pulls away before he can stop himself, and for a breath his hand has the sheen of the inside of a shell. |
| **6** | "My garden had a willow and a hawthorn." He runs his hand along the rail as he says it, as if the ship were one of them. |
| **7** | He names an island that isn't on any chart, then waves it off: "A story. Nothing more." |
| **8** | "Three hundred years," he says of a debt, then laughs it off as a figure of speech. |

**His true name.** No roll ever finds it; it comes out only in the reveal. If a player ever speaks it to him, he must answer one question with the plain truth. Unless it's used to help him, that player's favor drops to −3 for good.

## Running him in a fight

- **He doesn't join their fights.** The bargain counts only charts made by mortal choice, so he leaves the decisions, and the danger, to the crew.
- **If the ship is attacked,** the sea answers for him: a wave knocks boarders off the rail, the rigging tangles around an attacker, a sudden fog hides the ship. Use it to tip a fight, never to win it outright.
- **If someone attacks him,** blades pass through him like mist and spells unravel on his skin. He doesn't fight back. He's disappointed, which is worse. Favor drops to the bottom of the scale, −15, for whoever did it.
- **He has no hit points.** Nothing at their level can hurt him.

## No innocents aboard

**No innocent creature can be harmed on the Sallowmay.** It's the oldest law of his garden, the guest-law, older than the wager, and the ship carries it with her. Whether something is innocent is always your call.

### Fishing

When someone pulls up a fish (or a crab, or anything else), roll a die to see whether it was a good one or a bad one. A d6 works: **1 to 3, a bad fish; 4 to 6, a good fish.** Change the odds to suit the moment.

- **A bad fish** (a bully of the reef, one that ate its neighbors' eggs) can die, and it can be cooked and eaten.
- **A good fish** won't die and can't be killed, and it shows no sign of pain. The hook slides out without a mark, the knife won't cut, and it flops happily until someone throws it back.

### Food from shore

Meat bought for the ship's account comes only from animals that deserved it. The butcher doesn't know why he picks the ones he does, but he always has a story ready:

> "This pig? Mean as a snake. Bit my boy twice and chased the priest down the lane. Your captain's welcome to him."

### People

The same goes for people. Rescued sailors, a stowaway, a prisoner who has surrendered: no one can hurt them aboard. A blow meant for an innocent turns aside, a rope lets go, a deck plank tilts. Someone attacking the ship isn't innocent, so boarders can be fought as normal.

### Not the crew

**The law protects guests, and the crew aren't guests.** Passengers, rescued sailors, a stowaway, a fish pulled aboard: all guests. When the players took his hire, they signed on as crew, and crew are part of the ship. The ship takes her knocks, and so do they. If anyone asks:

> "You're not my guests. You're my crew. That's a different promise."

If a character ever quits the crew, the protection covers them again, because they're a guest once more.

### As a clue

This is one of the best clues the crew can find on their own: a fish that won't die, a knife that won't cut. If they ask the captain, he answers truthfully: "Nothing that doesn't deserve it comes to harm on my ship." Arcana DC 15 recognizes it as fae guest-law.

## His story

### The Lord of Far Shores

Calandrous Callomaydare was an archfey of the twilight courts, and he loved stories of the mortal world more than anything. He collected them the way other fae collect jewels: every coast, every harbor, every island anyone had ever sung about. He never traveled himself. He didn't need to. He boasted that no shore in the world was hidden from him.

### The wager

Three hundred years ago, at a midsummer revel by the sea, someone old and grey and patient was listening: Mother Brine, the oldest power of the sea, neither cruel nor kind. She offered him a wager. If he could name every island in her sea, she'd give him any one thing he asked. If he couldn't, he would owe her.

He named a thousand islands. She named one he'd never heard of: an island she keeps hidden, that no one has ever charted. He lost.

### The price

- He must sail her sea until **every coast in it has been charted by mortal hands** and given to mortal people.
- Until then, **he can't set foot on land.**
- **He can't draw the maps himself.** Fae ink won't hold a mortal coast; by morning the lines have wandered off the page. So he needs a crew.
- Only **charts made by mortal choice** count. That's why he lets the crew make every decision.

### The Sallowmay

The ship is the last piece of home he brought with him. She was grown, not built, from a willow and a hawthorn in his own garden. Sallow is an old word for willow, and may is the hawthorn's old name. That's why she never needs repairs: she heals. He loves her the way you'd love a dog that has followed you across the world.

### Three hundred years of crews

He has had many crews. Some grew old and went home. Some died, and he couldn't save them without breaking the rule. Some broke their word to him. He has learned to keep a little distance, and to let the crew make the choices, partly because the bargain demands it and partly because it hurts less.

He's quietly delighted by the Guild of Explorers: a whole guild of mortals paid to chart coasts. Every map they file counts toward his debt. It's why he sends his crews to them.

### The hidden island

Here's the catch he doesn't talk about: until the island Mother Brine named is charted, the debt can never be paid. He doesn't know where it is. Your campaign notes have "a place that isn't on any map" as an island idea. That's this island, and it's the campaign's ending: the crew finds it, charts it, and sets him free.

**It's hidden under stars (Joseph, 2026-10-09).** The night she won the wager, Mother Brine drowned a handful of stars in her sea. The island lies where they point. No one can see those stars any more, so no one can steer by them, and you can't see the island even from a mile off. You can only reach it by sailing the course they set.

- **The key is the Stargazer's spectacles.** They show the wearer the stars for 10 minutes a day, from anywhere, and that includes the drowned ones. Whoever wears them sees a small constellation of pale stars that's on no chart. Let the players name it.
- **Xuna is the one to wear them.** She's the navigator, and a Circle of the Stars druid, so her magic and the spectacles fit together. Ten minutes of stars a day gives one bearing a day, so the voyage is slow: a few days of sailing, a look through the spectacles, a correction to the course.
- **Lady Moreau has them (Joseph, 2026-10-09),** and she thinks they're broken: "Put them on and the room goes dark and fills with little lights. Ten minutes, then nothing until tomorrow. Charming. Useless." She bought them at a salvage auction, off a wreck no one could name. They sit in a glass case in her gallery, in plain view. She'd trade them for anything that glows.
- **What he knows.** He doesn't know about the drowned stars, and he's never heard of the spectacles. If they tell him, he goes very still. Slip 7 (he names an island no chart shows) is him guessing at it. He's guessed wrong for three hundred years.
- **Vesperine wants the spectacles lost** (see The rival's patron, below). If Rupert hears they exist, they become his errand.

### Signposting the spectacles

You don't know how many sessions the campaign will run, so tie the clues to **what happens**, not to session numbers. Plant the spectacles early, drop one clue each time the crew comes home, and pull the turn whenever you're ready to start the ending. A short campaign skips most of the clues; a long one spaces them out. Either way, the spectacles are already sitting where the players have seen them.

**1. Plant them early (the first time the crew visits Moreau Villa).** Lady Moreau offers 50 gold for the lantern, so the crew may meet her as early as Session 1. Put the spectacles in the case next to where the lantern would go. If anyone asks, she gives her "broken" speech and moves on to something that glows. That's all: no roll, no music cue. Let them forget about them.

**2. One clue per homecoming.** When the crew comes back to Kalatecha after an island, drop one of these, in any order. Skip any that don't fit, and stop when you've used enough.

| **Clue** | **Where it comes from** |
| "There used to be more stars over this sea. Ask anyone old enough." | Thimble, on a clear night at sea, out of nowhere. |
| An old sea-song: "Seven stars the Brine put out, and seven stars to steer by." Greta says her gran sang it, and nobody knows what it means. | Greta Vasquez, at her net loft. |
| The captain names an island that's on no chart, then says it's a story (slip 7). | An Insight win against him. |
| Fontaine shows them an old Guild chart with a blank patch every navigator avoids. Nothing has ever been found there, and no one can say why they steer around it. | The Charter House, when the crew sells a map. |
| Lady Moreau complains, at one of her parties, that the "broken" spectacles show the wrong sky: "Not one star I know." | Moreau Villa, if they bring her something that glows. |
| Xuna dreams of stars underwater. Story only: no roll and no rules effect. | Xuna, after a long rest aboard. |
| Nib is seen at Moreau Villa, or Rupert asks the Guild about Lady Moreau's collection. | Anywhere in the city. |

**3. The turn (when you want the ending to start, about two or three islands out).** Vesperine learns what the spectacles are, and Rupert goes after them. He tries to buy them first. If Lady Moreau won't sell, he sends Nib to steal them. Now the crew has to get them first, or get them back. This works the same whether it comes at session 6 or session 26.

- **If you're short on time:** let the crew trade Lady Moreau something that glows (the lantern, or the firebird feather if they freed it) before Rupert gets there. One scene.
- **If you have time:** Rupert gets them first, and getting them back is its own adventure: the Undaunted, Hargrove House, or wherever he's hidden them.

**4. The first look.** Someone puts them on and sees a small constellation of pale stars that's on no chart. Let the players name it. If it's Xuna, describe it as a constellation she feels she should have known all along. Then they show the captain, and he goes very still.

**5. The voyage.** One bearing a day, ten minutes at a time. That's the campaign's last voyage.

### What freedom would mean

He wants to walk on a beach again, feel sand, sit under a tree that isn't a ship. He's afraid he'll miss the sea, and the crew, and he'd never say so.

## The rescue and the reveal

Your notes set this up: if a character dies, he appears beside them out of thin air and brings them back. It's the only time he ever leaves the ship. Now it has a cost that ties into the backstory: **stepping off the Sallowmay breaks the terms of the wager, and Mother Brine takes her due.**

- **His price:** the glamour breaks for good. From then on the crew sees him as he really is. And Mother Brine hides one more island somewhere in her sea, so his debt just got longer (and the crew has a new place to find). He doesn't regret it.
- **The character's price:** as in your notes, a small fae mark, such as a silver mark on the skin or a favor owed. A good one: the revived character can now hear the sea talking, faintly, at night.

Read when he appears:

> The air beside you folds like a sail catching wind, and the captain is there, kneeling on the stones, which he has never once done. Salt water runs from his boots. Where his face was, there's something older: skin with the sheen of the inside of a shell, hair drifting as if underwater, eyes like the deep sea with light far down in it. He lays a hand on your friend's chest and speaks a word you feel in your teeth. Far away, the tide turns.

Then let him say his name, the whole of it, once.

## Hooks in play

Picked by Joseph, 2026-10-09.

### The rival's patron: Vesperine of the Thorn

Rupert Hargrove-Vance really is a warlock, and his patron is Vesperine of the Thorn, an Unseelie archfey of the twilight courts and the captain's rival for centuries. She collected mortal songs the way he collected mortal shores, and they tried to outdo each other at every revel. When he boasted that no shore was hidden from him, she was there. When he lost, she laughed loudest.

- **What she wants:** for him to stay lost: bound to the sea forever, and his place at court hers. So the crew must never finish a chart. She pays Rupert in luck to see to it.
- **How she found Rupert:** fifteen years ago, right after he broke his word to the captain (see Rupert and Fontaine's past). A man with a grudge against the Sallowmay was exactly the tool she needed.
- **Thimble knew her at court.** She won't say the name out loud. She calls her "the Thorn Lady," or just "her," and spits over the rail afterwards.
- **An open question:** did Vesperine invite Mother Brine to that midsummer revel? The captain has wondered for three hundred years. Whether it's true is your call.

### Rupert and Fontaine's past

Fifteen years ago, Rupert and a teenage Michael Fontaine crewed the Sallowmay together. That's the voyage that "went wrong": Rupert broke his word to the captain by selling a chart to someone other than the Guild. The ship's luck turned on him, and Vesperine found him soon after.

- It explains his grudge against the crew: they have the ship and the captain he lost.
- It explains why Fontaine trusts the captain without understanding him, and why he sends the crew to him.
- **The silver swirl on his neck** (Joseph, 2026-10-10). Before the voyage went wrong, the captain saved Rupert's life aboard the Sallowmay, the same way he brings Thimble back, and it left a swirl of silver on the side of Rupert's neck, just peeking out above his collar. Rupert knows the captain saved him, and never mentions it. A player who studies it can read it the way they'd read Thimble's spirals (Intelligence (Arcana), see Study her silver spirals): fae magic, the mark of being called back from very far away. A sharp player who has seen both may put Rupert's swirl and Thimble's spirals together.
- Fontaine won't talk about it at first. Pushed, he says: "Rupert made a promise to the captain and broke it. I've never seen luck turn on a man so fast."

### Two sprites

Rupert's familiar, Nib, from Pact of the Chain, looks like a sprite: it's a spirit wearing a sprite's shape, at a warlock's beck and call. It rides invisible on his collar. Its sheet is in the Library. Thimble is the real thing, and she can tell at a glance. It makes her furious. If the crew ever sees both together, a sharp player might notice the difference: one argues, one obeys.

### The firebird

It's caged in cold iron on Lantern Rock, the one thing the captain can't touch. He can't go there, and he won't ask, but he'll be very glad if they free it. The feather glows brighter when he's near.

### Small clues around the city

- **Greta's gran.** Ask Greta Vasquez about the captain and she says: "Green eyes? My gran used to talk about a captain with green eyes."
- **Sea-silver.** No one ever sees him pay for anything. Merchants who sell to the Sallowmay find old coins in their tills, salt-crusted, from wrecks no one remembers. Dario Benedetti has a jar of them.
- **The cathedral bells** (already in the city). Pip swears they rang by themselves the morning the crew notice went up, and they ring again when the ship leaves. It's not the captain's doing: it's Mother Brine noticing a new crew.

# Kalatecha City Guide

Oct 7, 2026 · Joseph Crook

## How to use this

Use this guide when the players wander off script in Kalatecha. If they head somewhere new, pick a place, give them a person to talk to, and roll on a table if you need something to happen. Every place and person has a rope back: a detail that points to Lantern Rock or to the captain, so wandering still moves the story forward.

Let them explore for 10 to 15 minutes, then use one of the pull-backs at the end of this guide to steer them to the next scene. Anything they buy for the captain or share with him counts as a gift on the favor track.

## Places

Eight places, the six from the campaign notes plus a tavern and a chandlery.

| Place | What's here | Something to do | Rope back to the plot |
| The Harbor ([[place:kcity/psallow|the Sallowmay]], [[place:kcity/pgreta|Greta's Net Loft]]) | Long piers, cargo cranes, a fish market, and old sailors mending nets. The Sallowmay is tied up at the end of the longest pier. | Watch ships come in, help unload cargo for a few coppers, or listen to Greta Vasquez's stories. | Greta says her grandmother called Lantern Rock's light "a light no human hand ever lit." |
| [[place:kcity/pbell|The Drowned Bell]] (tavern) | A noisy sailors' tavern on the waterfront, run by Marisol Ferro. One wall is covered with the names of ships that never came home. | Eat, swap stories, enter the sea shanty contest, try arm wrestling, or play liar's dice. | The three newest names on the wall are the Heron, the Marigold, and the Silver Tern. All three were lost near Lantern Rock this year. |
| [[place:kcity/padm|The Admiralty]] | The stone sea fortress. Armored guards, the harbormaster's office, and the city's cells. | Look at the ship registry, report a crime, or get arrested. | The registry shows that all three lost ships last logged a course past Lantern Rock. Commodore Quell also warns: "No ship has returned from the Ashen Isles." |
| [[place:kcity/pcharter|The Charter House]] | Headquarters of the Guild of Explorers: maps on every wall and a great half-blank globe. | Talk to Michael Fontaine, buy old maps, or look at the globe. | This is where the Lantern Rock job comes from (Scene 4). |
| [[place:kcity/pcath|The Cathedral]] | The great domed church with the tall bell tower. Sister Amara Bellweather heals here, and Pip Salazar rings the bells. | Get healed, buy potions, or ask for a blessing before the voyage. | Pip swears the bells rang by themselves the morning the Sallowmay's crew notice went up. |
| [[place:kcity/pmarket|The Market Square]] | Fruit and spice stalls, curio sellers, Old Tobias Pell and Admiral, and Madame Zisa's fortune-telling tent. | Shop, have their fortunes told, or chase Admiral. | This is where they find the lantern (Scene 2). Madame Zisa's fortune also points at Lantern Rock. |
| [[place:kcity/pchand|Benedetti's Chandlery]] | A cramped ship's supply shop near the docks, with rope, lanterns, tar, and weapons on the back wall. | Buy gear and weapons. | Dario Benedetti says the Sallowmay has never once come in for repairs, "not in all my thirty years." |
| The Upper Town ([[place:kcity/pmoreau|Moreau Villa]], [[place:kcity/phargrove|Hargrove House]]) | Villas on the terraced hills, with gardens, fountains, and gates. Home of Lady Celestine Moreau and Hargrove House. | Visit a rich sponsor, or snoop around Hargrove House. | Hargrove House's paint is peeling and the garden is overgrown, so Hargrove-Vance is broke. Somehow he still pays his crew. |

## People

Thirteen people the crew might meet. Each has a quick look and voice, what they want, and what they know.

| Who and where | Look and voice | Wants | Knows |
| [[npc:ln_fontaine|Michael Fontaine]], [[place:kcity/pcharter|Charter House]] | Tall, blond, early 30s, ink on his fingers. A former adventurer who is relieved to work behind a desk. | Lantern Rock solved, with no more lost ships on his record. | The commission details (Scene 4). He used to sail with Hargrove-Vance until a voyage went wrong. |
| [[npc:ln_tobias|Old Tobias Pell]] and Admiral, [[place:kcity/ptobias|Market]] | A jumpy little man. Admiral is a one-eyed gull that steals anything shiny. | To get rid of the lantern before trouble finds him. | The lantern came off a wreck on the southern reefs, sold by "people you don't want to meet." |
| [[npc:ln_hargrove|Rupert Hargrove-Vance]], anywhere ([[place:kcity/phargrove|Hargrove House]]) | Silver hair, a monocle, a Guild coat with the badges picked off, a swirl of silver just above his collar, and a journal of the crew's mistakes. | The lantern back, the firebird, and the Guild's respect. | Everything about the wreckers. He'll never admit it. |
| [[npc:ln_marisol|Marisol Ferro]], [[place:kcity/pbell|the Drowned Bell]] | A big laugh and strong arms, and she calls everyone "minnow." | For her wall of lost ships to stop growing. | The names of the lost ships, and that the Heron's captain was a friend of hers. |
| [[npc:ln_quell|Commodore Isadora Quell]], [[place:kcity/padm|the Admiralty]] | Iron-gray braid, clipped speech, and she never sits down. | Order in her harbor. | The ship registry, and the warning about the Ashen Isles. |
| [[npc:ln_okoro|Sergeant Bram Okoro]], City Guard ([[place:kcity/pcustoms|Customs Post]]) | A friendly giant who goes by the book. | A quiet shift. | Hargrove-Vance's deckhands have been starting fights on the docks all week. |
| [[npc:ln_amara|Sister Amara Bellweather]], the Cathedral ([[place:kcity/pinfirm|her infirmary]]) | Gentle, always humming, with flour on her sleeves from baking bread for the poor. | To send the crew off safely. | Heals for a donation, sells potions, and gives blessings before a voyage. |
| [[npc:ln_pip|Pip Salazar]], [[place:kcity/pbelltower|the bell tower]] | Ancient, half-deaf, and shouts everything. | Someone to believe him. | The bells rang by themselves the morning the crew notice went up. |
| [[npc:ln_greta|Greta Vasquez]], [[place:kcity/pgreta|the Harbor]] | Retired bosun with a wooden leg, mending nets. | A good listener. | Old sea sayings, including "never trust a light you didn't light yourself." |
| [[npc:ln_dario|Dario Benedetti]], [[place:kcity/pchand|the Chandlery]] | Fussy, with a measuring tape always around his neck. | Customers who don't haggle. | The Sallowmay has never come in for repairs. |
| [[npc:ln_moreau|Lady Celestine Moreau]], [[place:kcity/pmoreau|Upper Town]] | Glittering jewels, and bored by everything. | Rare and wondrous things for her collection. | She would pay a fortune for "anything that glows." She offers 50 gold for the lantern. |
| [[npc:ln_twins|Nico and Lina]], street kids ([[place:kcity/phideout|Under the Bridge]]) | Ten-year-old twins, barefoot and quick. They finish each other's sentences. | Coins and sweets. | Every alley in the city. They saw Hargrove-Vance's deckhands hiring toughs. |
| [[npc:ln_zisa|Madame Zisa]], [[place:kcity/pzisa|Market]] | Wrapped in scarves, she reads fortunes from tide shells. | A silver piece per fortune. | "You will follow a light that lies. Trust the one that doesn't." |

**If the crew sells the lantern to Lady Moreau,** they lose the flame that leans toward Lantern Rock, but they still have the Guild's chart. Let them choose. It's a good early taste of "free it or sell it."

## Things to buy

For ordinary gear like rope, rations, torches, and weapons, use the equipment prices in the Player's Handbook. Benedetti's Chandlery and the market have all of it. Below are the things only Kalatecha sells.

**The cathedral.** Sister Amara offers:

- Healing for anyone who's hurt, for whatever donation they can afford.
- A Potion of Healing for 50 gold pieces.
- A blessing before the voyage for a 5 gold piece donation. Each blessed character can reroll one d20 during the first voyage.

**The Drowned Bell.**

| Item or game | Cost | What happens |
| Bowl of fish stew and bread | 4 copper | Hot and filling. Marisol talks while they eat. |
| Mug of cider | 2 copper | Cold and sweet. |
| Sea shanty contest | Free | Performance check, DC 12. The winner drinks free all night and hears a rumor. |
| Arm wrestling | 1 silver bet | Athletics contest against a burly sailor. The winner takes the pot. |
| Liar's dice | 1 silver bet | Deception against the other player's Insight. The winner takes the pot. |

**Curios from distant islands.** Roll a d10 or pick one. These are sold in the market square.

| d10 | Curio | Price | What it does |
| 1 | A shell that whispers | 2 gp | It plays the sound of a different sea each day. Useless, and lovely. |
| 2 | Glow-moss in a jar | 5 gp | Gives dim light for a week, then dies if it dries out. |
| 3 | A compass that points to the nearest cat | 3 gp | Exactly what it says. |
| 4 | Tin of never-soggy biscuits | 1 gp | Ten biscuits that stay crisp even soaked in seawater. |
| 5 | A pearl with a tiny storm inside | 25 gp | Shake it and you hear thunder. |
| 6 | Fishbone flute | 2 gp | Fish swim toward the sound. |
| 7 | A mermaid's comb | 10 gp | Dries wet hair instantly. |
| 8 | A message in a sealed bottle | 1 gp | Written in a language no one in the city can read. Save it for a future island. |
| 9 | A carved wooden parrot | 15 gp | Repeats the last thing said near it, once a day. |
| 10 | A map fragment | 5 gp | Part of a coastline no one recognizes. Let the navigator add it to the map as a future island. |

## Loot and rewards

**Rewards for helping someone in the city.** Pick whatever fits:

- A handful of silver, from 2 to 5 pieces.
- A free meal at the Drowned Bell, whenever they're in port.
- A Potion of Healing from Sister Amara.
- A favor owed. The NPC will help them once, later.
- A curio from the d10 table.
- A rumor from the rumor table.

**What's in a stranger's pocket.** Roll a d6 if someone picks a pocket or searches a defeated bandit.

- 2d6 copper pieces.
- A lucky rabbit's foot.
- A love letter, unsent.
- A brass key to something.
- A pair of loaded dice.
- Half a pear.

**If they get caught stealing,** Sergeant Okoro hauls them to the Admiralty. The fine is 5 gold pieces or a night in the cells. Captain Callomay pays the fine without a word, and gives the thief a long look. Keep it light: a lesson, not a punishment.

## Rumors

Roll a d10 when the crew listens at the tavern, on the docks, or in the market. The DM-only column says whether a rumor is true.

| d10 | Rumor | True? |
| 1 | "Lantern Rock's light is a ghost looking for its ship." | False, but close. Something alive is up there. |
| 2 | "Those ships near Lantern Rock aren't sinking. Someone's taking them." | True. The wreckers. |
| 3 | "Hargrove-Vance hasn't had a Guild job in a year, but he's never short of gold." | True. He buys the wreckers' loot. |
| 4 | "No ship has ever come back from the Ashen Isles." | True. Save it for a future island. |
| 5 | "The Sallowmay's been tied up at that pier longer than anyone remembers, and her paint never fades." | True. A clue about the captain. |
| 6 | "A pirate queen rules the southern reefs and wears a crown of shark teeth." | Partly true. There is a pirate queen, Raven Heartgrove. The crown is up to you. |
| 7 | "The cathedral bells ring on their own when someone lucky comes home." | Up to you. Pip believes it. |
| 8 | "There's an island out there that only appears under a full moon." | A future island, if you want it. |
| 9 | "Fontaine and Hargrove-Vance used to sail together, until something went wrong." | True. Neither of them will say what. |
| 10 | "A sea serpent ate the Heron." | False. The wreckers took her. |

## Random city events

Roll a d8 if things go quiet or the players are stuck.

| d8 | Event |
| 1 | Admiral swoops down and steals something shiny from a player. They can chase him across the rooftops with an Acrobatics check (DC 12), or bribe him back with a fish. |
| 2 | A cargo net snaps and a crate of oranges spills down the hill. If the crew helps catch them, the merchant gives them a basket for the voyage. |
| 3 | A pickpocket brushes past a player. A Perception check (DC 13) catches Lina in the act. Caught, she offers to trade what she knows instead. |
| 4 | Guards march a half-drowned sailor to the cathedral. He was fished out of the bay last night and keeps shouting, "Don't follow the light!" |
| 5 | A sea shanty breaks out on the docks. Joining in (Performance, DC 10) earns a free round at the Drowned Bell and a rumor. |
| 6 | Hargrove-Vance's deckhands shoulder past the crew on purpose, looking for a fight. Good for setting up Scene 5. |
| 7 | A goat gets loose in the market and eats a player's hat or map. Catching it is a Dexterity check (DC 12). |
| 8 | A wedding procession crosses the square, and flower petals rain down. Whoever catches the bride's bouquet gets a kiss on the cheek from the bride's grandmother and a blessing for luck. |

## Names for people you make up

Mix and match a first name and a family name when the players talk to someone who isn't on the list.

| First names | Family names |
| Marco, Lucia, Tomas, Ines, Rafa, Bianca, Teodor, Sofia, Emilio, Carmen, Davi, Ysolde, Orsino, Paloma, Benedek | Corrado, Vela, Ruiz, Moretti, Santos, Delacroix, Brandt, Varga, Castell, Amaro, Lisboa, Pereira, Rossi, Duarte, Fennick |

Sailors often go by nicknames instead: Saltbeard, Two-Knives, Lucky, Gull, Patch, Old Barnacle.

## Pull-backs

When it's time to move on, use one of these to bring the crew back to the script:

- A Guild runner finds them: "Master Fontaine is waiting, and he is not patient."
- Nico and Lina run up: "Your captain says the tide turns at dusk!"
- Admiral steals something and flies straight toward wherever the next scene is.
- Hargrove-Vance's deckhands are spotted heading for the Sallowmay.
- The cathedral bells ring the hour, and they remember the ship sails tonight.

# DM Cheat Sheet: Checks and Things

Oct 7, 2026 · Joseph Crook

The rules you'll reach for most at the table, from the 2024 rules. Keep it next to the screen.

## Calling for a check

- **Only roll when failing would be interesting.** If anyone could do it, or failing changes nothing, just say yes.
- **Pick the ability and skill** from what the player describes doing, then **set a DC** from the table below.
- The player rolls a d20 and adds their modifier. **Meet or beat the DC to succeed.**
- A natural 20 or a natural 1 only means something special on **attack rolls**, not on ability checks.

| **Task difficulty** | **DC** | **Feels like** |
| **Very easy** | 5 | Almost anyone manages it |
| **Easy** | 10 | A little effort or luck |
| **Medium** | 15 | Needs some skill |
| **Hard** | 20 | Only a skilled character, on a good roll |
| **Very hard** | 25 | Exceptional |
| **Nearly impossible** | 30 | Legend-making |

## Advantage and Disadvantage

- **Advantage:** roll two d20s and use the higher. **Disadvantage:** roll two and use the lower.
- If something gives both, they cancel out. Several sources of Advantage still only means two dice.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** a reward you can hand out for great play. The player spends it to reroll any die right after rolling it, and must use the new roll.

## Which skill?

| **Skill** | **Ability** | **Use it for** |
| **Athletics** | Strength | Climbing, swimming, jumping, shoving through |
| **Acrobatics** | Dexterity | Balancing, tumbling, staying on your feet |
| **Sleight of Hand** | Dexterity | Pickpocketing, palming, quick fingers |
| **Stealth** | Dexterity | Sneaking and hiding |
| **Arcana** | Intelligence | Magic, spells, magical creatures |
| **History** | Intelligence | Past events, people, legends |
| **Investigation** | Intelligence | Working things out from clues |
| **Nature** | Intelligence | Plants, animals, weather, terrain |
| **Religion** | Intelligence | Gods, rites, holy symbols |
| **Animal Handling** | Wisdom | Calming or controlling an animal |
| **Insight** | Wisdom | Reading someone: are they lying? |
| **Medicine** | Wisdom | Diagnosing, first aid |
| **Perception** | Wisdom | Noticing things, finding hidden things (like loot on a body) |
| **Survival** | Wisdom | Tracking, finding the way, foraging |
| **Deception** | Charisma | Lying convincingly |
| **Intimidation** | Charisma | Threats and scaring someone |
| **Performance** | Charisma | Music, acting, storytelling |
| **Persuasion** | Charisma | Convincing someone honestly |

- **Searching vs studying:** the Search action is a Wisdom check (Insight, Medicine, Perception or Survival). The Study action is an Intelligence check (Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature or Religion). **Finding a hidden object is Wisdom (Perception)**, as long as they search in the right place.
- **Passive Perception** = 10 + their Perception bonus. Use it when they'd notice something without asking to look.

## Actions on a turn

| **Action** | **What it does** |
| **Attack** | Attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike |
| **Dash** | Extra movement equal to their Speed |
| **Disengage** | Their movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks |
| **Dodge** | Attacks against them have Disadvantage; their Dex saves have Advantage |
| **Help** | Help someone's ability check or attack roll, or give first aid |
| **Hide** | Dexterity (Stealth) check |
| **Influence** | Charisma or Wisdom check to change a creature's attitude |
| **Magic** | Cast a spell, use a magic item or a magical feature |
| **Ready** | Wait for a trigger they name, then act |
| **Search** | Wisdom (Insight, Medicine, Perception or Survival) check |
| **Study** | Intelligence (Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature or Religion) check |
| **Utilize** | Use a nonmagical object |

## In a fight

- **Opportunity attack:** when a creature they can see leaves their reach, they can use their Reaction for one melee attack, just before it leaves. Disengage avoids it, and so does teleporting or being moved without using their own movement.
- **Critical hit:** a natural 20 on an attack always hits; roll all the damage dice twice and add modifiers once. A natural 1 always misses.
- **Cover:** half cover +2 to AC and Dex saves, three-quarters cover +5, total cover can't be targeted directly.
- **Hiding:** DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth), only while heavily obscured or behind three-quarters or total cover. A hidden creature has the Invisible condition, and gives its position away when it attacks.
- **Can't be seen:** attacking a creature that can't see you is at Advantage.
- **Grapple or shove** (Unarmed Strike): the target makes a Strength or Dexterity save against DC 8 + the attacker's Strength modifier + Proficiency Bonus. Shove pushes 5 feet or knocks Prone.
- **Difficult terrain:** every foot of movement costs 1 extra foot.
- **Influence:** the DC is 15 or the creature's Intelligence score, whichever is higher.

## Dropping to 0 HP

- Monsters die at 0 HP. A character falls Unconscious and starts **death saving throws** at the start of each of their turns: d20, **10 or higher succeeds.**
- Three successes: stable. Three failures: dead. **Natural 20:** back up with 1 HP. **Natural 1:** two failures.
- Taking damage at 0 HP is a failure (two if it's a critical hit). If damage drops them to 0 and the leftover damage equals or beats their HP maximum, they die outright.
- Campaign note: a character's first death is when Captain Callomay appears.

## Conditions

| **Condition** | **Effect** |
| **Blinded** | Can't see; fails checks that need sight. Attacks against it have Advantage, its attacks have Disadvantage. |
| **Charmed** | Can't attack or harm the charmer. The charmer has Advantage on social checks against it. |
| **Deafened** | Can't hear; fails checks that need hearing. |
| **Exhaustion** | d20 tests –2 per level, Speed –5 ft per level. Level 6 is death. A long rest removes one level. |
| **Frightened** | Disadvantage on checks and attacks while it can see the source; can't move closer to it. |
| **Grappled** | Speed 0; Disadvantage attacking anyone but the grappler; can be dragged. Escape: action, Athletics or Acrobatics vs the escape DC. |
| **Incapacitated** | No actions, Bonus Actions or Reactions; can't speak; Concentration ends. |
| **Invisible** | Can't be seen. Attacks against it have Disadvantage, its attacks have Advantage. |
| **Paralyzed** | Incapacitated, Speed 0, fails Str and Dex saves. Attacks have Advantage; hits from within 5 ft are critical. |
| **Petrified** | Turned to stone: Incapacitated, Speed 0, fails Str and Dex saves, Resistance to all damage. |
| **Poisoned** | Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. |
| **Prone** | Crawl, or spend half its Speed to stand. Its attacks have Disadvantage; attacks from within 5 ft have Advantage, from farther Disadvantage. |
| **Restrained** | Speed 0. Attacks against it have Advantage, its attacks have Disadvantage; Disadvantage on Dex saves. |
| **Stunned** | Incapacitated, fails Str and Dex saves; attacks against it have Advantage. |
| **Unconscious** | Incapacitated and Prone, drops what it holds, fails Str and Dex saves. Attacks have Advantage; hits from within 5 ft are critical. |

## Out of a fight

- **Short rest:** 1 hour. They can spend Hit Point Dice to heal.
- **Long rest:** at least 8 hours. All lost HP and all spent Hit Point Dice come back, and Exhaustion drops one level.
- **Falling:** 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 feet fallen, up to 20d6.
- **Jumping:** long jump up to their Strength score in feet with a 10-foot run-up (half without). High jump 3 + Strength modifier feet with a run-up (half without).
- **Holding breath:** 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (at least 30 seconds).

## Looting in the app

- Nothing on a fallen enemy is found until someone searches. Pick who searches, type in their **Perception** total, and they find everything whose DC it meets.
- Weapons they fought with are in plain sight. Coins and carried things default to DC 10 (easy); change any item's DC on the card or in the Library.
- After the fight, the fallen stay at the place under Loot here, so the party can still search them later.

regions.name: Harbor District
regions.notes: Piers, the warehouses, the fish market, the Drowned Bell, and the chandlery. Rowdy after dark.

regions.name: Old Town
regions.notes: The waterfront market, the Charter House, the cathedral, and the lookout hill. Busy by day.

regions.name: Upper Town
regions.notes: Villas on the terraced hills. Rich sponsors, and Hargrove-Vance.

regions.name: The Admiralty
regions.notes: The stone sea fortress on the northern headland. Armored guards, the harbormaster, and the city's cells.

regions.name: Outside the City
regions.notes: Farms and olive groves inland. The roads get lonely.

nodes.name: The Admiralty
nodes.notes: The stone sea fortress on the northern headland. Commodore Isadora Quell, the harbormaster: iron-gray braid, never sits. Her registry shows all three lost ships last logged a course past Lantern Rock. Her warning: "No ship has returned from the Ashen Isles." The city cells are here. Caught stealing: 5 gp fine or a night in the cells.

bmap.name: The Admiralty
bmap.notes: Commodore Quell's sea fortress: the guard room, her office, the registry of every ship (all three lost ships last logged a course past Lantern Rock), and the city cells. Caught stealing: 5 gp or a night in a cell.

nodes.name: Watchtower
nodes.notes: The round tower at the tip of the headland. Guards watch every ship that comes and goes.

nodes.name: The Drowned Bell
nodes.notes: Sailors' tavern in the old warehouses, run by Marisol Ferro, who calls everyone "minnow." One wall lists ships that never came home; the newest are the Heron, the Marigold, and the Silver Tern, all lost near Lantern Rock this year. Fish stew 4 cp, cider 2 cp. Sea shanty contest, arm wrestling, liar's dice.

bmap.name: The Drowned Bell
bmap.notes: Marisol's tavern. The bar runs down the west side with the casks behind it and the kitchen past it; the names of ships that never came home cover the north wall. Shanty contest on the little stage; stairs up to the rooms.

nodes.name: Fish Market
nodes.notes: Loud, wet, and smelly. Gulls everywhere. A good place for random event 1 (Admiral steals something) or 5 (a sea shanty breaks out).

bmap.name: The Fish Market
bmap.notes: Loud, wet and smelly: fish laid out on tables, tanks of live catch, and gulls everywhere. Open to the quay on the south side.

nodes.name: Benedetti's Chandlery
nodes.notes: In the last warehouse at the head of the harbor. Rope, lanterns, tar, and weapons on the back wall. Dario Benedetti, fussy, tape measure around his neck. The Sallowmay has never once come in for repairs, "not in all my thirty years."

nodes.name: The Charter House
nodes.notes: Grand arched building facing the head of the harbor across the plaza. Guild of Explorers headquarters: maps on every wall and a great half-blank globe. Michael Fontaine gives the Lantern Rock commission here (Scene 4). Buy old maps; sell new ones.

bmap.name: The Charter House
bmap.notes: The Guild of Explorers: maps on every wall, half of each one empty, and the great half-blank globe in the middle. Michael Fontaine's office is in the corner.

missions.title: Chart a safe channel to Lantern Rock
missions.patron: Michael Fontaine, for the Guild of Explorers
missions.reward: 50 gold pieces each, a bonus for anything valuable brought back, and a copy of the Guild's chart
missions.text: Lantern Rock lies about two days' sail south. Its lighthouse has shone every night for as long as anyone remembers, though no one lives there, and ships that follow its light don't come back. Three have been lost this year. Wanted: a crew to chart a safe channel through the reef, and to find out what became of the lost ships.
missions.notes: Fontaine offers it in Session 1, Scene 4, with the sealed letter. A quartermaster's DC 15 Persuasion raises the fee to 60 gp each. The truth: wreckers use a caged firebird as a false light (see Lantern Rock). Set this to Taken when the crew accepts: Lantern Rock becomes a known route. Un-hide the reef in its own panel.

nodes.name: The Cathedral
nodes.notes: Great dome and tall bell tower, right behind the Charter House. Sister Amara Bellweather heals for a donation, sells Potions of Healing (50 gp), and blesses voyages (5 gp: reroll one d20 on the first voyage).

bmap.name: The Cathedral
bmap.notes: The great domed cathedral: rows of pews, pillars down the nave, the altar under the dome. The bell tower stands beside it (its own place); Sister Amara's infirmary is through the east door.

nodes.name: Bell Tower
nodes.notes: Pip Salazar, the half-deaf bell-ringer, swears the bells rang by themselves the morning the Sallowmay's crew notice went up.

nodes.name: Sister Amara's Infirmary
nodes.notes: Healing for anyone who's hurt, for whatever donation they can afford.

bmap.name: Sister Amara's Infirmary
bmap.notes: Sister Amara's infirmary: cots for the sick, shelves of herbs and potions (Potion of Healing 50 gp), and the oven where she bakes bread for the poor.

nodes.name: Market Square
nodes.notes: The market spills right along the east quay: fruit and spice stalls, crates, carts, and curio sellers (roll on the d10 curio table) beside the moored ships. Every merchant says the Sallowmay's supplies are "already settled." Scenes 2 and 3 happen here.

bmap.name: The Market Square
bmap.notes: The market square, loud and bright: stalls of fruit, spice and curios, the fountain in the middle. The cathedral's shadow falls across half of it; Old Tobias Pell's salvage stall is in the corner (Scenes 2 and 3).

nodes.name: Tobias's Stall
nodes.notes: At the edge of the square, in the cathedral's shadow. Old Tobias Pell sells salvage, including the lantern that burns without oil (10 gp). Admiral, his one-eyed gull, steals anything shiny.

nodes.name: Madame Zisa's Tent
nodes.notes: Fortunes read from tide shells, 1 silver each. "You will follow a light that lies. Trust the one that doesn't."

nodes.name: The Sallowmay
nodes.notes: Tied up at the end of the Long Pier. Every voyage begins and ends here. Captain Callomay never leaves her. Scrubbed deck, polished bronze fittings, not a scrap of iron. The crew-wanted notice is nailed to a post at the end of the pier.

nodes.name: The Undaunted
nodes.notes: The Undaunted's own berth at the Merchant Pier. When she's in port, Go aboard takes you onto her; her deckhands loiter here between jobs.

nodes.name: Greta's Net Loft
nodes.notes: Greta Vasquez, retired bosun with a wooden leg, mends nets here and tells stories: "Never trust a light you didn't light yourself." Her grandmother called Lantern Rock's light "a light no human hand ever lit." Scene 5's dock fight happens along the quay out front.

nodes.name: Lookout Steps
nodes.notes: The hill on the south side of town. The city picture is the view from here: the harbor on the left, the fortress on the far headland, the cathedral dome, and the terraced hills on the right. Worn stone steps lead down to the quay, and armored guards often stand watch. A good spot to show the players the picture.

nodes.name: Moreau Villa
nodes.notes: Lady Celestine Moreau collects rare and wondrous things. She'd pay a fortune for "anything that glows" and offers 50 gold for the lantern.

bmap.name: Moreau Villa
bmap.notes: Lady Celestine Moreau's villa: a gallery of rare and wondrous things in glass cases, her salon, and a grand hall for parties. She'd pay 50 gold for the lantern.

nodes.name: Palm Terraces
nodes.notes: Terraced palm gardens high on the hill, with fountains and a view over the whole harbor. A good place to spot the Sallowmay, or the Undaunted, from above.

nodes.name: Hargrove House
nodes.notes: Rupert Hargrove-Vance's villa. The paint is peeling and the garden is overgrown, so he's broke, yet he still pays his crew. Snooping here can turn up a ledger of payments to "friends on the southern reefs."

bmap.name: Hargrove House
bmap.notes: Rupert Hargrove-Vance's villa: peeling paint, an overgrown garden, and still somehow the money to pay his crew. In the study, his ledger of payments to "friends on the southern reefs" (DC 15 to find).

nodes.name: Customs Post
nodes.notes: A toll booth where the Inland Road leaves town. Sergeant Bram Okoro of the City Guard often stands watch here.

bmap.name: The Customs Post
bmap.notes: Sergeant Okoro's post on the road out of town: a counter for tolls and papers, a small office, and one cell.

nodes.name: Under the Bridge
nodes.notes: Nico and Lina's hideout under the Inland Road bridge over the Brightwater. The twins know every alley, and they saw Hargrove-Vance's deckhands hiring toughs. They'll trade information for coins and sweets.

bmap.name: Under the Bridge
bmap.notes: Nico and Lina's hideout under the Inland Road bridge: bedrolls, a crate for a table, and their stash in a tin (they'll trade what they know for coins and sweets).

nodes.name: Olive Farm
nodes.notes: Farmland and olive groves inland. Not part of Session 1, but here if the players wander out the Inland Road.
Old stone warehouse on the north shore.
Old stone warehouse on the north shore.

nodes.name: Shipwright's Yard
nodes.notes: Slipways and timber stacks on the south shore. They build and mend every ship in the harbor, except the Sallowmay, which has never needed them.

bmap.name: The Shipwright's Yard
bmap.notes: Where ships are built and mended: a new hull on the slipway, stacks of timber, a crane, and the workshop. The Sallowmay has never once been here.

nodes.notes: Fishing boat.
Fishing boat.
Fruit and spice stall.
Curio stall. Roll on the d10 curio table.
Fish and bread stall.

nodes.name: Dockworkers' Shed
nodes.notes: Where the dock hands rest between ships. Ask here for work loading cargo, a few coppers a crate.

nodes.name: Dock Ambush (Scene 5)
nodes.notes: Where Hargrove-Vance's deckhands jump the crew on the way back to the ship. Sample fight: six deckhands, a Low warm-up for a level-3 party of four.

nodes.name: Visitors' Berth
nodes.notes: Where visiting ships tie up on the Cargo Pier: the first ship in port without a berth of her own takes it, one at a time.

shapes.name: Kalatecha Harbor
shapes.notes: The harbor basin, sheltered by the fortress headland to the north. Open sea to the west.

shapes.name: Fortress Wall
shapes.notes: The Admiralty's walls run from the round watchtower east along the northern ridge, up into the terraced hills.

shapes.name: The Terraces
shapes.notes: Terraced hills with palms and villas, climbing behind the red-tiled rooftops. The Upper Town sits here.

shapes.name: Lookout Hill
shapes.notes: The hill the city picture is drawn from.

shapes.name: The Plaza
shapes.notes: The paved plaza between the head of the harbor and the Charter House.

shapes.name: Brightwater
shapes.notes: A small river that runs down from the inland hills, around the south side of Lookout Hill, and into the harbor.

shapes.name: The Quay
shapes.notes: The east quay. The dock fight in Scene 5 happens along here.

shapes.name: Long Pier
shapes.notes: The longest pier in the harbor.

shapes.name: The Steps
shapes.notes: Worn stone steps up to the lookout.

shapes.name: The Switchback
shapes.notes: A zigzag stair up the terraced hill.

shapes.name: Inland Road
shapes.notes: The road out of town toward the farms. It crosses the Brightwater on a stone bridge.

regions.name: The Rock
regions.notes: Bare stone, the landing and the lighthouse crag. Wreckers watch from the gallery.

regions.name: The Ship Graveyard
regions.notes: The lagoon of wrecks. The octopus hunts here.

regions.name: Wreckers' Cove
regions.notes: The pirates' camp in the sea cave under the north cliffs.

nodes.name: The Shingle Landing
nodes.notes: The only safe place to come ashore: a steep bank of shingle on the east side, reached by the channel through the reef. Rowboats from the Sallowmay beach here. From here a goat-narrow path climbs the bare rock to the lighthouse. If the ship followed the false light instead, this is where a scraped hull limps in.

nodes.name: The Lighthouse
nodes.notes: A tall, salt-scoured tower on the island's high crag. Its light has shone every night for as long as anyone remembers, and no one lives here. There is no oil store, no wick, and no keeper's cot: the first clue. Inside, a spiral stair climbs round a stone core. Wreckers hold the stair: the first half of the big fight. At the top is the Lantern Room.

bmap.name: The Lighthouse
labels: the stair climbs round and round
bmap.notes: The base of the tower. The spiral stair (the U squares) climbs round the stone core to the Lantern Room. The stair is narrow: the wreckers come at the crew a few at a time.

nodes.name: The Lantern Room
nodes.notes: The top of the lighthouse, reached only by its spiral stair. The firebird is locked in a cold-iron cage where the lamp should be, and a gallery with a low rail runs all round, high over the sea. Raven Heartgrove and Hargrove-Vance are haggling over the firebird when the crew arrives: the second half of the big fight. Swing from the great lamp's chains; knock pirates off the gallery into the sea. Hargrove-Vance slips away rather than fight.

bmap.name: The Lantern Room
labels: a long drop to the sea
bmap.notes: The lantern room at the top of the tower. The firebird is in its cold-iron cage in the middle. The door on the east side opens onto the gallery and its low rail, high over the sea. The crew comes up the stair at the U.

nodes.name: Wreck of the Marigold
nodes.notes: Lost this year (her name is on the Drowned Bell's wall). Stripped bare: her cargo crates turned up stenciled MARIGOLD in the Undaunted's hold. Gouges in her hull show where the wreckers pried her open.

nodes.name: Wreck of the Heron
nodes.notes: Lost this year, beached on her side at the head of the lagoon. The young stowaway hides in her hold, living on hardtack and rainwater, and has watched the wreckers come and go.

nodes.name: Wreck of the Silver Tern
nodes.notes: The newest and biggest wreck, broken on the reef at the lagoon's mouth, her hold half-flooded. The giant octopus lives in it. Salvage worth taking is still aboard.

bmap.name: Wreck of the Silver Tern
bmap.notes: The Silver Tern lies broken-backed on the reef, her middle stove in and flooded. The giant octopus waits in the flooded hold and grabs anyone at the edge. Salvage is still in the stern.

nodes.name: Sentry's Perch
nodes.notes: A wrecker sentry under a scrap of sailcloth on the west arm, watching the reef for ships. A brass bell hangs from a spar: if the sentry rings it, the cove is warned. Sneaking past or silencing the sentry is its own small challenge.

nodes.name: Wreckers' Cove
nodes.notes: A sea cave under the north cliffs, reachable by boat at low water or down a hidden stair from the lighthouse crag. The wreckers' camp: beached longboats, plunder, bedrolls round a fire, a pen of captured sailors held for ransom, and the queen's nook with the strongbox. The crew can sneak in, bluff, or fight.

bmap.name: Wreckers' Cove
bmap.notes: The wreckers' camp in the sea cave: longboats drawn up on the sand, plunder stacked by the wall, bedrolls round the fire. The captured sailors are in the barred pen (south-west). The queen's nook is in the south-east, with the strongbox. The party starts where a boat comes in at the cave mouth; the hidden stair from the crag comes down by the pen.

shapes.name: The Southern Reefs
shapes.notes: Open sea all round. The reefs make every approach but one deadly.

shapes.name: Lantern Rock
shapes.notes: Bare, jagged stone, scoured by salt and wind. Hardly a blade of grass. The high crag in the north-west carries the lighthouse; the two arms in the south hold the lagoon.

shapes.name: The Ship Graveyard
shapes.notes: A sheltered lagoon full of wrecks: three lost this year and older hulks under them, green with weed. A giant octopus lives in the biggest.
Steep grey shingle. The one safe landing.
A strip of coarse sand at the head of the lagoon.

shapes.name: Graveyard Reef
shapes.notes: Across the lagoon's mouth. The Silver Tern broke her back on it.

shapes.name: The Western Teeth
shapes.notes: The reef the false light leads ships onto.

shapes.name: Northern Reef
shapes.notes: Shuts off the north-east. Longboats can slip through at low water; a ship can't.
A sea stack, white with gulls.
A sea stack.

shapes.name: The Cliff Path
shapes.notes: A goat-narrow path over bare rock, from the landing up to the lighthouse door. Exposed the whole way: anyone on the gallery can see who's coming.
A scramble down from the cliff path to the lagoon's sand.

shapes.name: The Wreckers' Stair
shapes.notes: A hidden stair cut in the rock from the lighthouse crag down to Wreckers' Cove. Easy to miss: Wisdom (Perception) DC 15, or the stowaway can show them.

regions.name: The Sallowmay
regions.notes: The captain's ship, grown from a willow and a hawthorn. No innocent can be harmed aboard.

nodes.name: Captain's quarters
nodes.notes: His cabin at the stern. Roomier inside than it looks from the deck. The ship's log is on the desk; under the bunk, a sealed scallop shell. Searching it counts as prying if he finds out (he will).

bmap.name: The Sallowmay: captain's quarters
bmap.notes: His cabin, roomier inside than it looks from the deck: his bed under the stern windows, a side table and wardrobe, charts on the shelves, the desk with the ship's log on it, a small table for two, a sea chest. Three lamps. The ship's log is in the desk (DC 15); a sealed scallop shell is under the bed (DC 20).

nodes.name: Below decks
nodes.notes: Down the ladder through the hatch: the crew's hammocks, the galley (brick and bronze, no iron) and the hold. The masts run down through it to the keel.

bmap.name: The Sallowmay: below decks
bmap.notes: Below decks: the crew's hammocks, the galley (brick and bronze, no iron) with its table, the hold with crates, barrels and sacks, and the masts running down to the keel. No daylight reaches here: four lamps swing from the beams.

nodes.name: Main deck
nodes.notes: Scrubbed white, ropes coiled neat as sleeping snakes, every fitting bronze. The captain is usually at the rail, Thimble on his shoulder.

bmap.name: The Sallowmay: main deck
bmap.notes: The Sallowmay's main deck, scrubbed white, every fitting bronze. Lamps hang by the cabin door, at both masts, at the bow and by the hatch; the cabin door leads to the captain's quarters, the hatch down below decks.
